votes.reason: Traced exactly as described. SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1806 `SSRPurgeChart(0, SSR_PICK_LINE)` is unconditional and is the second statement of OnInit; SSR_Widgets.mqh:676-694 enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and deletes every object whose name starts with "SSR" except the single `keep` name (SSR_PICK_LINE, SSR_Theme.mqh:508). Both handoff objects are SSR-prefixed and created on chart 0 (SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF, #define at 536, created in StashOrigin; SSR_PICK_HANDOFF created at ~2536). ReadStashedOrigin() runs 63 lines later at 1869 and ObjectFind(0,SSR_PICK_STASH) at 1884 - both after the delete, in the same invocation. So on pass 2 stashed=="" -> origin=="" (1903) -> the on_replay&&origin=="" branch at 1911 -> FailInit(), whose restore branch is gated on g_origin != "" and therefore does nothing. No guard, clamp or earlier check anywhere prevents this; the outcome holds whether or not objects survive ChartSetSymbolPeriod. With the shipped default InpOneChart=true this makes every one-window run fail on the pass that owns the replay chart and strands the user on a custom-symbol chart with no expert.

Provable from source with no runtime assumption required. SSRPurgeChart (Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:675-693) enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and deletes every object whose name satisfies StringFind(nm,"SSR")==0 unless it equals the single `keep` argument, which is SSR_PICK_LINE (Ui/SSR_Theme.mqh:508). Both handover objects match that prefix - SSR_HANDOFF="SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF" (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:536) and SSR_PICK_STASH="SSR_PICK_HANDOFF" (556) - and both are created on chart 0 (540, 2536), the same chart the sweep runs on. The sweep is at line 1806, unconditional; ReadStashedOrigin() is at 1869 and ObjectFind(0,SSR_PICK_STASH) at 1884, i.e. 63 and 78 lines later in the same invocation of OnInit. So `stashed` is always "", origin is "" at 1903, the guard at 1911 fires, and FailInit() (824-836) cannot restore the chart because its own guard tests g_origin != "". MQL5 semantics do not rescue this: ObjectGetString on a non-existent object cannot return the text, and whether chart objects survive ChartSetSymbolPeriod is irrelevant because the delete and the read are in one pass of one function. Corollary I verified while judging the rest of the batch: because `stashed` is always empty, the "!"-poison branch at 1894-1900 is also dead, so one_chart_ok can never diverge from InpOneChart anywhere in the program.

Verified end to end. SSRPurgeChart (Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:676-694) enumerates ObjectsTotal(chart,-1,-1) and ObjectDelete()s every name where StringFind(nm,"SSR")==0 except the single keep argument, which here is SSR_PICK_LINE. SSR_HANDOFF=="SSR_ORIGIN_HANDOFF" (mq5:536) and SSR_PICK_STASH=="SSR_PICK_HANDOFF" (mq5:556) both match that prefix and are both created on chart 0 (540, 2536). The sweep is at 1806, unconditional, and ReadStashedOrigin() is at 1869 in the same function - 63 lines later. So on pass 2 stashed=="", origin=="" at 1903, the guard at 1911 fires and FailInit() returns INIT_FAILED; FailInit's restore branch at 825 requires g_origin!="" and is therefore skipped, leaving the user's chart pointed at a custom replay symbol with no expert and no automatic way back. This is the shipped default (InpOneChart=true, InpPickStart=true), so it is not an edge case - it is every normal run. Impact lens: the product does not function at all in its default configuration and it damages the user's workspace on the way out; the picked start and the '!' poison die in the same sweep, so neither the chosen window nor the two-window recovery path survives either. The claim also does not depend on whether chart objects survive ChartSetSymbolPeriod, because the delete and the read are in the same pass of the same function.

votes.reason: Traced: OnInit:1893 sets `one_chart_ok = InpOneChart` and the only thing that clears it is the '!' poison branch (1894-1901). Pass 2 therefore enters BuildSession with on_replay=true AND one_chart_ok=true, so the guard at 1710 `if(InpAutoPlay && !one_chart_ok)` is false and the else branch prints 'auto-play waits for the handover' on the pass that IS final. g_group.Play() at 1712 is the file's only Play() call site (grep confirms lines 1710-1724 are the only AutoPlay sites), and the refused-handover recovery path at ~2650 does not play either. The correct predicate is expressed correctly twice elsewhere (1276, 1689-1694) as `one_chart_ok && !g_on_replay_chart`. So in the default configuration auto-play never fires.
votes.corrected_claim: Correct as a defect in the condition, but currently unreachable as user-visible behaviour: pass 2 dies at origin=="" (host-expert-1) before reaching line 1710. It becomes live the moment host-expert-1 is fixed. Consequence is a motionless chart plus a false log line, not data loss - HIGH overstates it.

votes.reason: The two mechanisms are provable. (a) CSSRRandomPicker::SetSeed is `m_seed = (s == 0 ? SSRPickSeed() : s)` (SSR_RandomPicker.mqh:68-69) and SSRSeedFromText("") returns 0 (SSR_Random.mqh:94-100), so pass 2 with g_setup_ready false re-rolls a brand-new seed and picks a different window; if the pick lands on another instrument, BuildSession reassigns origin/g_origin (1027-1035) while the sink is pinned by SetAdoptName(_Symbol) (1964) and CSSRCustomSymbolSink::Prepare prints a warning and adopts the existing name anyway (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:152-166) - confirmed, a chart named for one instrument carrying another's prices. (b) The pass-2 inheritance block (1935-1947) assigns twelve fields from inputs and omits random_start and seed, whose Init() defaults are false/"" (SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:144-146), so InpRandom/InpSeed cannot reach a restored setup. Nothing carries random_start/PickedStart across the handover.
votes.corrected_claim: Case (b) is narrower than stated: CSSRSetupPanel::Restore DOES read 'random' and 'seed' from setup.ini (SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:1258-1259), so randomness is switched off only when the stale file holds random=0 or lacks the key (which is the common case, because the setup form's own defaults at 2044-2068 never seed random_start/seed from InpRandom/InpSeed either). Both cases are also currently unreachable: pass 2 fails at origin=="" (host-expert-1) before BuildSession is entered.

The pass-2 block at 1932-1947 assigns twelve fields from inputs and omits random_start and seed; SSRSetupValues::Init() leaves them false/"" (Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:139-146). CSSRSetupPanel::Restore does not fall back to the Init() defaults for random/seed in practice: Save always writes the `random` and `seed` keys (Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:1230-1231), so Restore reads them from the file (1257-1258) and the Init() false/"" values only act as defaults for a truncated file. The defect is the same either way - InpRandom and InpSeed are discarded on pass 2 and replaced by an unrelated earlier run's file values - but the mechanism is "the file wins", not "the struct default wins".

CSSRSessionDialog::OnEvent begins `if(m_mode == SSR_SD_CLOSED || id != CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK) return false;` (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:227-228), so a keydown is never claimed and RouteEvent's dialog block at 3167 falls through; the range-dialog block behaves the same. Control therefore reaches 3228 g_panel.OnEvent, which for CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN maps the key with SSRKeyToCommand, returns false only for the four commands Owns() excludes (SSR_Panel.mqh:2165-2177: NONE/SESSIONS/JUMP/REVIEW/REPLAY_FROM_HERE) and otherwise runs Execute(c); Render(); return true (2855-2876). Render() recreates the panel's objects, and creation order is the only z-order, so it reprints over the open dialog. The timer already computes the right predicate at 3052 (`modal`) and uses it for PollClicks and Render, but RouteEvent does not.

The key-routing half is provable. CSSRSessionDialog::OnEvent returns false unless id==CHARTEVENT_OBJECT_CLICK (Ui/SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:227-228) and CSSRRangeDialog::OnEvent handles only OBJECT_ENDEDIT/OBJECT_CLICK (Ui/SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:258+), so a CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN passes both blocks at 3160-3195 unclaimed. votes.reason: Confirmed by trace. CSSRChartManager::OpenChart (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) is an unconditional ChartOpen + NoteOwned with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period, and OpenLayout (229-242) just loops it. The only close site in the whole Chart tree is CloseOwned (line 292; grep for ChartClose finds no other), and OnDeinit calls it only inside `if(user_removed)` at 2202-2206, so REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all leave the windows open while the replay symbol is deliberately kept. The next pass's manager is a fresh object, so the old ids are no longer in m_owned and Sync (332-377) only discovers and policies them - it never closes. CSSRLeakGuard::Scan (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:44-63) only counts. So each non-removal re-init opens a new replay window plus one per InpExtraTfs entry and orphans the previous set.

Verified. OnDeinit's only close sites are inside `if(user_removed)` at 2201-2211, and user_removed covers REMOVE/PROGRAM/CLOSE only, so REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all skip CloseOwned. CSSRChartManager::OpenChart (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) is an unconditional ChartOpen + NoteOwned with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period, and OpenLayout (229-242) loops it. Crucially I confirmed the ownership gap the claim rests on: Sync() registers a rediscovered chart with Add(id) only (332-351), never NoteOwned, and CloseOwned closes m_owned exclusively (278-306) - so windows left by a previous instance are tracked but can never be closed by any later pass. Add() also returns -1 past SSR_MAX_CHARTS (82-83), so surplus windows drop out of the follow policy as claimed. The INIT_FAILED leak is sound under MQL5 semantics: OnDeinit runs with REASON_INITFAILED after OnInit returns a non-zero value, which is outside the user_removed set.

Confirmed from source on all three legs: OnDeinit's only close sites are inside `if(user_removed)` (2203/2206) and REASON_CHARTCHANGE, REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_RECOMPILE and REASON_INITFAILED all fall outside it; CSSRChartManager::OpenChart is an unconditional ChartOpen + NoteOwned with no search for an existing chart on that symbol/period (Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:204-215) and OpenLayout just loops it (229-242); CloseOwned walks m_owned (278-306), which a freshly constructed manager on the next pass no longer holds; and the destructor is empty (139). Reachable without any other fix: in two-window mode (InpOneChart=false, a configuration a user can and does pick) simply clicking OK in the inputs dialog raises REASON_PARAMETERS and orphans the previous replay window, and the same happens on every recompile. Kept at MEDIUM rather than raised: the leak is visible - stale windows on a replay symbol the user can close by hand - and costs no money arithmetic or data integrity; kept at MEDIUM rather than lowered because it accumulates silently, the orphans keep showing a frozen replay that looks like the live session, and past SSR_MAX_CHARTS the newest windows also drop out of the follow policy.

votes.reason: Trace holds. ReportSpreadOnce() is called at 2458, before the g_picking block at ~2470, and g_timer_ticks++ is the first statement of OnTimer, so it counts picker ticks; the picker arms a 200 ms timer at 2072. At 500 ticks (100 s) the condition `total < 120 && g_timer_ticks < 500` fails, g_spread_reported is set true at 2263, and with the controller unloaded total==0 and EffectiveFidelity defaults to SSR_FIDELITY_SYNTHETIC_TICK (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:69-73, and SpreadBarsRecorded/Fixed forward to the synthesizer counters via SSR_ReplayController.mqh:657-658) so the 'no bar has been replayed yet' branch prints. grep shows g_spread_reported has exactly two occurrences (2232 declaration, 2263 assignment) - no reset anywhere, and BuildSession resets only g_timer_ticks (1577). The build happens in the same program instance, so the latch is already spent when the real session starts.

Verified by grep: g_spread_reported occurs exactly twice in the file - declared at 2232, set true at 2263 - with no reset anywhere, while BuildSession resets g_timer_ticks at 1577. ReportSpreadOnce() is the second statement of OnTimer (2458), before the g_picking block at 2470, and g_timer_ticks is incremented unconditionally at 2454. The picker arms a 200 ms timer at 2072, so g_timer_ticks reaches 500 after 100 s of picking with the controller unloaded (SpreadBarsRecorded/Fixed forward to the synthesizer's zeroed counters, Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:657-658), total==0, the latch is set and the session's one spread diagnostic is spent on a message about a replay that has not started. Which of the two total==0 branches prints depends on the unloaded controller's EffectiveFidelity(), but the latch is set either way, so the outcome does not turn on that.

Confirmed: ReportSpreadOnce() is OnTimer's second statement (2456), ahead of the g_picking block at 2465; the picker runs the timer at 200 ms (2072); the latch condition at 2260 releases once g_timer_ticks reaches 500, i.e. 100 s of picking, with the controller unloaded so recorded+fixed==0; g_spread_reported is assigned at 2263 and, per grep, is never reset anywhere, while BuildSession resets only g_timer_ticks (1577). So a user who takes more than 100 s to choose a start loses that session's spread line and gets the misleading 'no bar has been replayed yet' instead. Impact is confined to one diagnostic log line: nothing the engine does changes, the spread actually used is unaffected, and the same facts are still visible on the panel's fidelity indicator. LOW is right (borderline IMPROVEMENT); the reason it is not dismissed is that this line is the one the file itself designates as the evidence to send when reporting a fault, so losing it costs a support round trip.

votes.reason: The arithmetic defect is provable. t0 is declared ulong at 651 while GetTickCount() returns uint, so at 653 the fresh uint is widened rather than wrapped and `GetTickCount() - t0` after a wrap underflows in 64-bit to a value near 2^64, which is >= 60000 and ends the loop. The same pattern is wrap-safe elsewhere in the file because both operands are uint (2894 with `uint now_ms`, 3145 with g_ready_at_ms declared uint at 345). GetTickCount64() is the wrap-free primitive and is not used here.
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism is real but the claim's probability framing is wrong. The wrap must fall inside the loop's own lifetime, not merely on a terminal that has been up for weeks - roughly a 60 s window in each 49.7 days, i.e. ~1e-5 per download - and the realistic effect is an early exit part-way through a download (EnsureHistory falls out of the loop and prints its normal tail line), not a systematic no-op that never enters the body.

votes.reason: The type error is real and provable. GetTickCount() returns uint and wraps every 2^32 ms (~49.7 days of terminal uptime); t0 is declared ulong at 651, so in `(GetTickCount() - t0) < 60000` at 653 the fresh uint is zero-extended to ulong before the subtraction instead of wrapping modulo 2^32. The file writes the same idiom correctly everywhere else with uint operands - `uint now_ms = GetTickCount(); ... now_ms - g_panel_paint >= 100` at 3062-3063 and `(GetTickCount() - g_ready_at_ms) > 1500` at 3146 with g_ready_at_ms declared uint at 350 - so 651 is the lone outlier, and GetTickCount64() is the wrap-free primitive. Consequence as described: if the wrap falls between t0 and a loop test the budget evaluates as exhausted, the download is abandoned, and BuildSession's SHORT ON HISTORY cascade at 1109-1123 then blames the broker. Severity stays LOW - the vulnerable window is roughly the 60 s preceding a wrap that occurs once per 49.7 days of uptime.

A grep of the whole tree finds CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE written only in Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh (318 save, 324 set true inside Create, 370 restore), and Create is reached from the host at 1467 - after the picker has returned INIT_SUCCEEDED at 2073. CSSRSetupPanel::Create (SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:481-) touches only CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL (970, 983), never the event property. Panel.Destroy restores the prior value, so an earlier session does not leave it enabled. The host's forwarding call at 3117 is correctly placed ahead of the g_ready gate, so forwarding is not what blocks it - the chart simply never emits the event. Buttons still work because the timer polls OBJPROP_STATE, so the failure is silent as described.

Text(12,"setuprow",x+8,gy+12,...) at :1402 and Text(17,"setuprow",x+8,gy+12,...) at :1432 write the SAME object id at the SAME coordinates; I grepped the slot numbers and 17 is used nowhere else, so m_cache[17] holds order_why persistently. votes.reason: Traced the whole FULL_TICK branch and found no guard anywhere on the path. SSR_ReplayController.mqh:334-369: the ONLY degradation trigger is `tp == NULL` (337-346). With a live provider, `n = tp.ReadTicks(...)` is taken at face value: CSSRMt5TickProvider::ReadTicks (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:401-470) returns 0 (not -1) for a range the broker holds no ticks for — `if(got == 0) break;` — so n==0 is not an error, EmitTicks/PublishTicks are skipped by `if(n > 0)`, and line 367 `m_cursor.Advance(hi, 0, 0)` unconditionally consumes the window before `return emitted`. No bar provider is consulted, no PublishBar, no SetTicksAvailable(false), no log line. m_ticks_available is written in exactly two places (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:344 and 806) and CSSRTickProvider::HasTicks has zero callers anywhere in MQL5/ (grep: only its declaration and the Mt5 implementation), so availability is never re-evaluated per window. The upstream chain is as claimed: SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:133-139 sets has_ticks from a CopyTicksRange probe of the last 24h of held data only, and SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153 requests FULL_TICK whenever range.has_ticks. Progress/Publish still advance (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:172-186), so the clock and the panel keep moving over a market that emits nothing. There is no `n == 0` branch, no bar fallback, no log, and the only degradation trigger is `tp == NULL` (337-346). CSSRMt5TickProvider::ReadTicks (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:410-472) returns 0 and calls Succeed() when CopyTicksRange yields `got == 0` (line 442-443 `if(got == 0) break;`), so a tick-less window is indistinguishable from a quiet one at this layer. Ticks() is offered whenever m_has_ticks (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:93-96), and m_has_ticks comes from Discover's probe of only the last 24 h of held data (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:133-139: `from_msc = to_msc - 24*60*60*1000`), while the host pins FULL_TICK off that same flag (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153). Clamped to POTENTIAL_RISK for one reason only: manifesting requires a broker whose stored tick depth is shorter than its M1 depth, and how MT5 answers CopyTicksRange for a range outside the server's tick retention (0 vs a -1/ERR_HISTORY_LOAD that the retry loop at 425-440 would turn into an error) cannot be settled from this source. votes.reason: Traced both the publish surface and the consumer. Observers are reached only through PublishBar/PublishTicks/PublishSegment/PublishRewind (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:189-236), and the only callers of the first three are inside EmitWindow (366, 506-515). JumpForward's bulk leg (1370-1392) calls m_sink.SeedBars + m_metrics.RecordSeed + m_cursor.Advance(last_bar-1, 0, n) and nothing else; only the target's own bar goes through EmitWindow (1395-1402), and when the target is a bar open the keep filter leaves exactly the i=0 tick. CSSRTradingEngine evaluates AccrueSwap/CheckPendings/CheckStops/CheckStopout only inside OnTicks (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:600-613); OnBarContext merely caches (593-598) and OnClock only bumps m_now_msc (616-617). StepBackward reaches this via RestoreSnapshot -> PublishRewind (which un-does the stop-out, SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:634+) then JumpForward(target) at 1458, so the bars between checkpoint and target are replayed blind to the account — exactly the described chart/account divergence, for every '<-' press, GotoBookmark -> JumpTo, forward J-jump and RestoreFrom's JumpTo(want_now) at 1826. Nothing compensates: the host's only post-jump repair is PrimeView() for the strategy market view (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2794-2798), which does not touch the trading engine.

Correctly LOW: emission still follows m_fidelity.Decide(), so playback fidelity itself is unaffected — only what is shown and saved.

SSRReplayState carries fidelity, speed_x100, status, last_error and last_error_text (SSR_ReplayState.mqh), TakeSnapshot copies the whole struct (out.state = m_state, line 1598), and RestoreSnapshot assigns it back wholesale at 1630 — after ClearError() at the top of the method, so a snapshotted last_error is reinstated. CSSRFidelityPolicy is a separate member and is not restored, while SetFidelity writes both (671-676), so m_state.fidelity and m_fidelity.Requested() diverge exactly as claimed; the accessors the UI reads sit on opposite sides of that split (Fidelity() returns m_state.fidelity at line 628, EffectiveFidelity() returns the policy's m_effective at 685, and SSR_GroupPort.mqh:110-111 reads both into the panel). votes.reason: The strict comparison and the coincidence it fails on are both provable. CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Truncate floors to the M1 open, CustomRatesDelete/CustomTicksDelete from that instant inclusive, and returns bar_open (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:712-744) — matching the contract text at SSR_IReplaySink.mqh:46-59 ('everything at or after from_msc must cease to exist'). Pump emits PendingRange(now) with hi == now and advances the cursor to it (1015-1017, 531) before TakeSnapshot sets taken_at_msc = m_clock.now_msc (1598), so snap.cursor.emitted_msc == snap.taken_at_msc. When taken_at is exactly an M1 open, actual == emitted and the `if(actual < m_cursor.emitted_msc)` at 1637 does not fire, so the cursor keeps claiming an instant whose tick was just deleted; the next EmitWindow's keep filter (`t < lo`, 462-464) drops the i=0 tick, whose time_msc is exactly base_msc and whose bid is bar.open (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:148-152). The bar therefore rebuilds from the second synthetic tick (base + span/(n-1) = +8571ms at 8 ticks) and its open no longer matches the broker's. Contrast is correct: SeekTo (1233) and Reset (1286) call RewindTo(actual) unconditionally. votes.reason: The finding's core premise is that the engine's own synthesised tick order is evidence about what happened. The file states the opposite at lines 11-20 ('that ORDER IS OUR ASSUMPTION, not the market's behaviour'), and it is true: an M1 bar cannot say whether the minute's low printed before or after the instant the user clicked Buy mid-minute, so for a mid-minute entry whose stop sits under that minute's low the outcome genuinely is unknowable and the pessimistic-plus-flag policy (R11) is exactly what is documented. The one case where unhappened price would be used is already guarded twice: ClipBar (ReplayController 240-279) rebuilds a forming bar from only the ticks up to the pump window end, and BarIsAmbiguousFor 156-158 rejects a cached bar the current tick does not live in. 'Every synthesised tick after the entry was above the stop' is precisely the self-flattery the design refuses, and the trade is flagged rather than silently booked, with AmbiguousPercent reporting the fraction. No defect provable from source; at most a possible refinement (weighting by entry time within the minute), which would itself require inventing intra-minute order.

The code path is provable: BarIsAmbiguousFor (141-175) tests p.sl/p.tp against m_bar.low/m_bar.high with no reference to open_msc, to the ticks already seen, or to the running mae (which UpdateExcursions 293-300 already maintains), and CheckStops (537-541) routes any touched level through it, booking ClosePosition(i, StopFill(i), SSR_CLOSE_SL, true). The bar it tests is the whole minute up to the pump window end - ClipBar (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:269-300, called at 459) deliberately rebuilds the shown bar from the bar's own open, 'the window's LOWER bound is deliberately not applied' - so a low printed in an already-emitted segment, before the position existed, still makes a later TP hit book as a stop loss. Reachable in the stated way (SYNTHETIC_TICK is the automatic fidelity whenever the broker has no real ticks, SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153-1154) and user-visible: the chart the user watched shows price never returning to the stop after their entry, yet the journal records SL and marks the trade ASSUMED. Not upgraded past MEDIUM because the loss is flagged rather than hidden and the mid-bar entry instant itself sits on the synthesised timeline, so some pessimism here is defensible; the defect is its extent, not its existence. The fill-time half of the claim (371-384) only sets an honesty flag and moves no money.

OpenWithRisk/OpenPendingWithRisk (759-801) add only lot-sizing checks. FreeMargin() (946) and MarginLevel() (949) exist but no caller in the engine or in GroupPort/Publisher/Strategy gates an entry on them, and CheckStopout (436-470) runs from OnTicks 613 only after the fill, so the oversized position is charged round-turn commission (BookExit 203) and slippage (StopFill/FillPrice) before being force-closed as SSR_CLOSE_STOPOUT with m_stopouts++ (464). Margin modelling is opt-in (InpMarginLot default 0.0, SSReplayStandalone.mq5 94-95), which bounds the blast radius but does not refute the path.

The absence is provable: Open() 705-756 performs no affordability test, OpenWithRisk/OpenPendingWithRisk 759-801 add only sizing checks, FreeMargin() (946) has no production caller anywhere in the tree (only SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5 461 reads it), and CheckStopout 436-470 runs from OnTicks 613 only after the fill has been booked and its commission taken at 753-754. So with margin modelled, an order that a terminal would refuse with 'not enough money' at zero cost is instead accepted, charged entry commission, then force-closed by CheckStopout at FillPrice(...,false) with a second commission and adverse slippage, incrementing m_stopouts and tripping the SSR_PAUSE_ON_STOPOUT announcement. Severity cut from MEDIUM: the whole path needs two non-default inputs (InpMarginLot > 0 and InpStopout > 0, both default 0.0 at host lines 94-95), and MarginModelled() is explicitly an opt-in model.

votes.reason: Both halves of the claim fail. (1) Semantics: SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL is defined by MT5 as the amount in the margin currency required to open ONE LOT - it is not contract size, and when a symbol publishes it the terminal uses it instead of the contract-size/leverage formula. votes.reason: Both branches the claim rests on are arithmetically impossible. ViewOffset = first-(visible-1) with a `off<0 -> 0` clamp (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:124-125). At the right edge under CHART_SHIFT, whichever way MetaTrader defines CHART_VISIBLE_BARS, first_visible_bar can never EXCEED visible-1: if `visible` is window capacity in bar slots and the shift gap eats G slots, first = visible-G-1 so off = -G -> clamped to 0; if `visible` counts only slots holding bars, first = visible-1 so off = 0 exactly. There is no 'systematically positive' branch, so the 'permanent false detach on every chart' outcome cannot occur. The 'clamped to 0' branch is also not the described defect: Redraw's snap is gated on `ViewOffset(...) > 0` (line 575), the SAME clamped number, so inside the dead zone the snap does not fire either - the tool does not 'keep yanking the user back'. The shift merely inflates both the detach threshold and the snap threshold by the same G bars, and because one formula feeds both they stay consistent by construction (the finding cites that shared use as an aggravator; it is the mitigation). What is genuinely wrong is only the doc comment at lines 111-113, whose premise ignores the CHART_SHIFT set at line 315.

The contradiction is real in source: ApplyPolicy (line 315) sets CHART_SHIFT=true on every chart, including on discovery (line 367), while ViewOffset's premise (111-116) assumes bar 0 sits at the right border. Under the documented reading of CHART_VISIBLE_BARS ("number of bars that CAN be displayed" = window slot capacity), the shift consumes ~CHART_SHIFT_SIZE percent of those slots, so at the right edge first < visible-1 and `off` is negative, clamped to 0. But the finding's two claimed outcomes do not follow. (a) The "systematically positive -> permanent false detach" branch is arithmetically impossible: under the alternative reading (visible counts only slots holding bars) off is 0 or 1 at the right edge, and DetectScroll requires off > SSR_SCROLL_DETACH_BARS (3), so no detach. (b) "Redraw keeps yanking the user back" is wrong: Redraw's snap at line 574-575 is gated on ViewOffset(...) > 0, so inside the dead zone it does not fire at all. The residual effect cannot be settled from source because it depends on MetaTrader's runtime definition of CHART_VISIBLE_BARS under CHART_SHIFT and on the terminal's CHART_SHIFT_SIZE (never set by this code, so the user's default applies).
votes.corrected_claim: ViewOffset's stated premise assumes bar 0 sits at the right border, which ApplyPolicy's CHART_SHIFT=true prevents. Under MetaTrader's documented CHART_VISIBLE_BARS semantics (window slot capacity) the resulting offset at the right edge is negative and clamped to 0, creating a dead zone roughly equal to CHART_SHIFT_SIZE percent of the window: a scroll-back smaller than that reads as offset 0, so DetectScroll never detaches and native CHART_AUTOSCROLL (still on) keeps pulling the user forward - the UX the feature exists to prevent, for small scrolls only. Redraw does not contribute (its snap is gated on offset > 0), and a permanent false detach is not reachable by this arithmetic. The magnitude, and whether it happens at all, depend on runtime CHART_VISIBLE_BARS semantics that no spike or test in the tree measures.

CSSRChartManager exposes no deletion entry point - the only ClearMarks() in the tree is CSSRSnapshotStore::ClearMarks (SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:191), which clears a counter, not objects. ObjectsDeleteAll is called for exactly two prefixes (SSR_CalendarLines.mqh:116, SSR_Widgets.mqh:639), neither of which matches. In one-chart mode the marks land on the EA's own chart (Sync matches on symbol alone, line 344, and g_replay_chart == ChartID() at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1276); OnDeinit hands that chart back with ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period) at 2192 rather than closing it, and chart objects outlive a symbol change, so the OBJ_VLINEs persist on the user's live chart. OBJPROP_HIDDEN=true (line 184) does suppress them from the terminal's object list. Severity reduced to LOW: the residue is cosmetic and carries no data or trading consequence.

Verified by exhaustive grep: "SSR_MARK_" appears at exactly one place in the tree, the creation site (SSR_ChartManager.mqh:170); there is no ClearMarks/ObjectDelete path for it. The only ObjectsDeleteAll calls in production are SSR_CAL_PREFIX (SSR_CalendarLines.mqh:116) and CSSRWidgets::RemoveAll with each component's own prefix - the panel's is "SSRP_" (SSR_Panel.mqh:276), which does not prefix-match "SSR_MARK_", so no purge reaches these objects. In one-chart mode Sync matches on symbol alone (line 344), so the host chart is registered and MarkTime draws on it; teardown hands that same chart back to the origin symbol (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2194 ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period)) rather than closing it, and MQL5 graphical objects are chart-bound, not symbol-bound, so the OBJ_VLINEs survive the symbol change and are saved with the chart. votes.reason: Traced end to end and confirmed. Scan() increments other_live_charts for any chart that is neither the replay nor the origin symbol and is not a replay symbol (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:59-60), but SSRLeakReport::IsClean() tests only origin_in_watch and origin_charts (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:105-108), Advice() returns "" whenever IsClean() (SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:91-92), SSRLeakReport::ToString() short-circuits to the literal 'no leak' on the same test (line 115-116), and SSR_GroupPort.mqh:167-169 copies only LeaksClean()/LeakAdvice() into the port, which SSR_Panel.mqh:1892-1894 renders as T(SSR_S_CHARTS_CLEAN) = 'clean'. grep confirms other_live_charts has no reader outside the increment, the struct and the log-only ToString at line 104, and ENUM_SSR_LEAK::SSR_LEAK_OTHER_SYMBOL_CHART is never assigned anywhere. Severity LOW rather than higher: a correlated instrument is a judgement call the guard cannot make (it has no correlation input), so the defensible fix is surfacing the count, not folding it into IsClean.

The factual half is verified - other_live_charts is incremented at line 60 and read only by ToString() (line 104), and ENUM_SSR_LEAK::SSR_LEAK_OTHER_SYMBOL_CHART is never assigned - but the defect framing does not hold. IsClean() (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:105-108) deliberately scopes a leak to the ORIGIN symbol, and that is the only scope the code can justify: Scan() counts every chart whose symbol is neither the replay symbol nor the origin nor a replay symbol (SSRIsReplaySymbol), which includes any unrelated instrument a trader happens to have open for other work. Nothing in this class measures correlation, so the finding's "highly correlated instrument" is an inference the code has no basis for; folding other_live_charts into IsClean() would make the panel declare a leak on essentially every real desktop and would drown the origin-symbol warning it exists to deliver. The residue is an unused struct field plus unused enum vocabulary, i.e. an improvement, not a bug.
votes.corrected_claim: other_live_charts and ENUM_SSR_LEAK::SSR_LEAK_OTHER_SYMBOL_CHART are computed/declared but never consumed - dead measurement and dead vocabulary. IsClean()'s exclusion of them is defensible, not a defect: the scan cannot distinguish a correlated instrument from any unrelated chart the user has open, so promoting the count to a leak would fire on nearly every desktop. Either surface it as a neutral informational count or delete the field and the enum value.

votes.reason: The observations are accurate - other_live_charts is incremented at line 60, appears only in ToString (which the Expert never prints) and the struct, and IsClean (SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:105-108) tests origin only - but the scope is deliberate and correct. IsClean is documented as the origin-symbol contract, and the leak guard's whole subject is the instrument being replayed: it can act on that one (HideOrigin) and can act on nothing else, as the file header says up front. Counting every non-replay chart as dirty would mark essentially every real terminal permanently dirty - any watchlist chart, any unrelated pair - which turns the only leak indicator into noise the user learns to ignore, a strictly worse outcome for the blindness guarantee than the present origin-focused signal. Nor is this future data of the replayed series: a live correlated chart the user opened themselves shows today's price of a different instrument, and the panel's 'clean' is a statement about the origin, not a claim that the desk contains no live prices.

The only path that can carry a typed Balance to 'go' is step 1 -> next (ReadAll at :1063) -> step 2 -> next -> step 3, and step 3's RenderStart prints the parsed value back: Recap("bal2", "Balance", DoubleToString(m_v.balance,2)) at :879, alongside Risk/Speed/Evaluation. The quick paths (qlast/qcont/qrand) have no Balance box at all, so Num() returns its fallback (:286-287) and nothing is truncated there. Comma-as-decimal is a deliberate convention for this field, and the wizard's whole step-3 purpose is this read-back, so the described silent 1000x loss is not silent on the only path that can produce it.

votes.reason: The unreachability is provable from source. OnChartEvent returns immediately for anything but CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE (:958), and a grep over MQL5/** shows the only writer of CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE is CSSRPanel::Create (SSR_Panel.mqh:324), with CSSRPanel::Destroy restoring the saved value (:370) - so nothing leaks. The setup panel is created on ChartID() during the picking phase (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2069, inside OnInit before BuildSession) and destroyed on 'go' (:2522), while g_panel.Create runs later at :1467; the two lifetimes do not overlap, so the property is off (platform default) for the whole life of the setup panel and no CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE is delivered. Consequently SavePlace() (:1006-1011) never runs, SSR_SETUP_X/Y never exist, m_placed stays false and Create re-centres every run (:531-541). The secondary point is also correct but moot: :970 would set CHART_MOUSE_SCROLL true unconditionally, in code that cannot execute. Severity downgraded from MEDIUM: the pick line is a full-height OBJ_VLINE that can be grabbed above or below the panel, so this is a dead feature and a lost preference, not a blocked workflow.
votes.corrected_claim: Dead code rather than a malfunction: the caption-drag handler and SavePlace/m_placed path are unreachable because no code enables CHART_EVENT_MOUSE_MOVE on the host chart while the setup panel exists, so the panel cannot be moved and always re-centres - the picking workflow itself still works because the vertical pick line is grabbable outside the panel's footprint.

votes.reason: Traced and reproducible from source. m_menu is cleared only in DrawMenu when the option list is empty (:625), after a choice (:1092) and by the four field toggles (:1100-1103); for "pre" MenuOptions always returns at least 1 (slot 0 "My last"), so it never self-clears. Neither Repaint (:656-662) nor the next/back handlers (:1061-1074) reset m_menu or m_menu_y, m_menu_y is written only by Row() (:221-222) which runs from RenderSettings alone, and Render() calls DrawMenu last on every step (:673). Poll checks 'next' BEFORE the menu block, so a Next press while a list is open is honoured and the list is re-created on the new step. Geometry confirms the harmful overlap on step 3: menu items at x m_x+208..292, y m_y+291..391 (fy = m_menu_y + 20 + 1 with m_menu_y = m_y+270) versus go at x m_x+92..292, y m_y+316..342 (:939-943). DrawMenu runs after RenderStart, so the items are the later-created objects and win the click; Pressed("go") at :1076 is false and the menu block at :1084-1096 then applies a preset instead of starting. Minor nuance: on the MODE step the list falls just below the 288 px frame rather than over its buttons, which is cosmetic; the START-step capture is the real defect.

The stale-menu leak is provable. m_menu is assigned at only four sites (:625 empty-option list, :1092 after a choice, :1100-1103 the field toggles); neither Repaint() (:656-662) nor the 'next'/'back'/'md*' handlers clear it, and Render() calls DrawMenu() unconditionally as the last act of every paint (:673). m_menu_y is written only in Row() (:221-222), which runs only from RenderSettings, so it keeps the step-1 value across steps. Geometry checks out: Row("pre") is r = 10, ry = m_y+270, fy = m_y+291 (:629), five entries (1 "My last" + 4 built-ins) x 20 px = m_y+291..391, while RenderStart's back/go sit at gy = by+42 = m_y+316 (:939-941) and RenderMode's frame ends at m_y+288 - so the list is painted over the START row and, on step 2, floating below the panel. Poll does check those items on the later steps (the loop runs whenever m_menu != "", :1084-1096, and MenuOptions("pre") still returns five), so a press that lands on one applies a preset and returns "" instead of starting.
votes.corrected_claim: An open dropdown survives Repaint() and every step change (m_menu is never cleared by a step handler), so Render() repaints the preset list over the MODE and START steps, overlapping back/go at m_y+316. Which object consumes a click in that overlap is the one part not settleable from source: the menu buttons and the 'go' button both carry OBJPROP_ZORDER 100 from CSSRWidgets::Common (SSR_Widgets.mqh:164), and MQL5's tie-break between equal-ZORDER objects is runtime behaviour. If the later-created menu item wins, the press applies a preset and the replay does not start; if 'go' wins, the replay starts with a stray list on screen. Either way the stray menu itself is a confirmed paint defect.

votes.reason: Every link in the chain is present in source. CSSRBlindMode::Apply (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:147-176) records m_had_dates/m_had_ohlc/m_had_price only when Find(chart_id) < 0, and Find scans only the live instance's m_id[0..m_saved). The record has no persistence: a repo-wide grep for CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE / CHART_SHOW_OHLC / CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE matches only this file and the QA smoke test - no session-file field, no terminal global. OnDeinit (SSReplayStandalone.mq5) computes `user_removed = (reason == REASON_REMOVE || REASON_PROGRAM || REASON_CLOSE)` and calls g_blind.RestoreAll() only inside that branch (line 2176), so REASON_CHARTCHANGE / REASON_PARAMETERS / REASON_RECOMPILE tear the instance down with the chart still blinded. The rebuild then re-runs BuildSession, which calls SetPolicy (1002) and Apply on every synced chart (1421-1430); with m_saved back at 0 the already-hidden properties are recorded as the originals, and Restore (184-186) later writes those falses back. Chart properties are terminal state and outlive the program, so the true 'before' values are unrecoverable. The one runtime dependency is MQL5 reinitialising program globals across a deinit/init cycle, which is standard terminal behaviour rather than broker-specific; on that basis I cannot refute it.

The control flow is provable. OnDeinit computes user_removed = (REASON_REMOVE || REASON_PROGRAM || REASON_CLOSE) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2152-2153) and calls g_blind.RestoreAll() only inside that branch (2176), so REASON_CHARTCHANGE / REASON_PARAMETERS / REASON_RECOMPILE leave the chart blind. Nothing persists m_had_dates/m_had_ohlc/m_had_price: they are plain member arrays (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:117-119), CollectSettings writes no such field, and a repo-wide grep shows CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE / CHART_SHOW_OHLC / CHART_SHOW_PRICE_SCALE are touched only in SSR_BlindMode.mqh and the QA smoke script. The global CSSRBlindMode is reconstructed on reload with m_saved = 0 (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:131), so Find(chart_id) < 0 and Apply() records the already-hidden values as the originals (152-164) - the exact failure the boxed comment at 143-145 warns about, defended against only within one instance's lifetime. I also checked the branch the finding does not mention: if the rebuilt pass never reaches BuildSession, SetPolicy is never called, IsOn() is false and RestoreAll() restores nothing, so the chart stays blind anyway. Both branches end with the user's date scale, OHLC and price scale off. Residual runtime dependence is only that a chart's display properties outlive an EA reload, which is standard MT5 chart-level state and is the same assumption the class itself is built on.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate. votes.reason: Traced and confirmed, including the control flow the claim depends on. RestoreAll (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:200-210) clears m_applied but never touches m_policy, and the class exposes no Off()/ClearPolicy() - only SetPolicy, called once in BuildSession (Expert:1002). IsOn() returns m_policy.AnyOn() (line 136). In the pump function I verified there is no top-level function boundary and no bare `return` between line 2715 and line 3070, so the housekeeping block and the reveal block are in the same pass: `g_slow_tick++; if(g_slow_tick % 5 == 0){ ... if(g_blind.IsOn()) for(bi...) g_blind.Apply(g_charts.IdAt(bi)); ... }` sits at 2806-2825, outside the `if(playing)` guard at 2784-2789, and tests IsOn() rather than IsApplied(). Nothing in that block consults g_revealed (grep shows g_revealed only at 278, 2998, 3006, 3020). So the reveal at 3021 restores the scales and the next 5th tick re-hides them; with InpPumpMs defaulting to 40 (line 78) that is ~200 ms. Apply also re-saves the freshly restored values, so the record stays correct and final removal does restore properly - the defect is that the reveal payoff is undone, not that the chart is damaged.

I verified both halves of the asymmetry the finding rests on. RestoreAll() clears m_applied but never touches m_policy (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:200-210), and the class exposes no way to clear the policy - SetPolicy is the only mutator (134) and is called once, in BuildSession (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1002). IsOn() returns m_policy.AnyOn() (136), not m_applied. The housekeeping block gated on `g_slow_tick % 5 == 0` re-applies on IsOn(), not IsApplied() (2807-2824), and I checked it is outside the `if(playing)` guard (the guard closes at 2790 after g_group.Pump) and that no earlier `return` in OnTimer fires for a COMPLETED session - the early exits are g_picking, g_switching, the g_switch_to handover and !g_ready only. The reveal at 3021 calls RestoreAll() later in the same OnTimer body than the re-apply at 2824, so the restore survives to the end of that tick and is undone on the next pass with %5==0 - about 200ms at InpPumpMs = 40. g_revealed latches (3020), so the card never returns and the chart stays blind until REASON_REMOVE reaches 2176. Apply() does re-save the freshly restored values (152-164), so the record stays honest while the visible state flips back, exactly as claimed. Only the precise interval is runtime-dependent; the undo itself is not.

votes.reason: All three code sites verified. Leaks() (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:238-250) gates the price clause on `!m_policy.hide_price_scale`, and Full() sets hide_price_scale = true (line 79), so in SSR_BLIND_FULL the returned string mentions only the crosshair date and Market Watch/Navigator - the price is absent from the disclosure. Meanwhile CSSRTradeLines builds `tip = StringFormat("%s %s at %s", side, DoubleToString(volume,2), DoubleToString(entry, m_digits))` and passes it as both tooltip and label to Level(base+"_E", ...), and Level sets OBJPROP_TEXT to that string, with Attach forcing CHART_SHOW_OBJECT_DESCR true (line 183) precisely so it renders without hovering; SSR_Panel.mqh:1478-1487 formats the buy/sell buttons with Price(m_state.ask) / Price(m_state.bid) with no blind-mode routing. CSSRBlindMode's only masking helpers are MaskTime and MaskSymbol, neither of which touches price formatting. The defect is a real incompleteness in a disclosure string the class header explicitly commits to.
votes.corrected_claim: Leaks() does not assert that the price is hidden; it omits the price clause in FULL mode, which under the class's stated ethic (list every leak it cannot close) understates what remains visible - the absolute price is still shown on the panel's Buy/Sell buttons at all times and permanently on each position's entry-line description once a trade is taken. Category is better described as incomplete-disclosure / blind-mode leak than future-data-leakage: no future data is exposed, only the price level that identifies the period.

votes.reason: Leaks() does branch on !m_policy.hide_price_scale (SSR_BlindMode.mqh:245-247), so under SSR_BLIND_FULL - where Full() sets hide_price_scale = true (79) - the price clause is suppressed and no other string in the class mentions price. Meanwhile the absolute price is printed on two channels I verified directly. CSSRTradeLines builds `tip = StringFormat("%s %s at %s", side, volume, DoubleToString(entry, m_digits))` and puts it on the entry line's description and tooltip (SSR_TradeLines.mqh:413-422), with CHART_SHOW_OBJECT_DESCR forced true in Attach (183); the class holds no reference to blind mode. And the panel formats Price(m_state.ask)/Price(m_state.bid) into the Buy and Sell button captions (SSR_Panel.mqh:1478-1486) through a helper that only picks a digit count (266-271). The port hands those through unmasked - CSSRGroupPort's blind block rewrites only clock_text and symbol (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:180-184) while out.bid/out.ask come straight from the account (263-264). One correction: the deal buttons are drawn inside SheetTrade, so they are visible on the Trade tab rather than 'unconditionally' - which does not rescue the finding, since that is the tab a trader uses. Given the class's stated ethic of naming what it cannot hide (233-237), the omission is a real disclosure defect.
votes.corrected_claim: Correct, with one narrowing: the Buy/Sell price captions are drawn by SheetTrade, so they appear on the Trade tab rather than on every panel frame; the trade-line entry description (SSR_TradeLines.mqh:413-422) is the channel that is unconditional once a position or pending order exists.

votes.reason: Both halves verified. Leaks() (238-250) emits the price-level clause only `if(!m_policy.hide_price_scale)`, so FULL - where Full() sets hide_price_scale = true - silently drops it, i.e. the disclosure implies the price is covered. votes.reason: The absence of prop persistence is real (no SaveInto/RestoreFrom in SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh; no prop slot in CSSRSessionManager l.74-76/106-108), but the described outcome is prevented by a guard the finding never traces. Restore ends with m_group.At(i).NotifyRestored() (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:380-381) which is PublishRewind(now) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1668-1669), and g_prop is an observer of that controller (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1200, added before the Restore at l.1483). CSSRPropEvaluation::OnRewind (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:440-452) therefore fires and sets m_state = SSR_PROP_VOID with a reason and m_pause_pending, so the run is NOT silently RUNNING and is NOT re-anchored: the l.360 guard (state != RUNNING) makes every later OnClock return immediately, so the m_started re-anchor at l.365-376 never executes. Nor is it re-anchored during the wind-forward - OnClock is published only from Pump/PumpTo (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1029, 1104), never from JumpTo/JumpForward. The panel is fed prop_state/prop_state_name/Headline() (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:206-210), and Headline() returns "VOID - ..." (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:314-316), i.e. explicitly not authoritative; the host even prints "a rewind voids the run - that is deliberate" at init (l.1201-1203). Residual, and not what was claimed: a mid-session load while the live run is already PASSED/FAILED leaves that stale verdict standing, because OnRewind returns early for a non-RUNNING state.

Provable from source: CSSRSessionManager holds only group/account/stats pointers (l.74-76, Attach l.106-108), writes only [session]/[settings]/[stream]/[bookmarks] plus m_acct.SaveInto and m_stats.SaveInto (l.194-200), and grep confirms CSSRPropEvaluation has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom - the only SaveInto implementations in the tree are TradingEngine, StatsEngine and ReplayController. The host calls g_prop.Reset() once at init (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1197) before Restore (l.1483), and Reset() sets m_state back to SSR_PROP_RUNNING and zeroes m_trading_days/m_total_days (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:327-341), so a run saved as FAILED/PASSED does come back RUNNING and day counting restarts.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate except for two details: (a) the re-anchor branch is guarded by `if(!m_started)` (SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:366-378), not by `m_first_day == 0`; (b) the whole path only exists when the evaluation is enabled - g_prop is only added as an observer under `if(CfgProp())` (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1199-1200), so with prop mode off there is nothing to lose. Severity lowered to MEDIUM: this is unimplemented persistence on an opt-in feature rather than corruption of data the file already carries.

votes.corrected_claim: The operation count is smaller than claimed: the reachable worst case is ~8,760 entries, not 12,800, giving roughly 512x8,760 + 4,096x8,760 + 4,096x8,760 = ~76 million key comparisons (plus the three Count() passes), and a typical session (tens of trades, hundreds of equity samples) is three to four orders of magnitude cheaper. votes.reason: Traced the whole path. CSSRPanel::Text() (SSR_Panel.mqh:190-207) takes its fast path ONLY when m_cache[slot]==text && m_cache_x/y match && m_w.Exists(id), and on that path it *writes* OBJPROP_COLOR every time - so the object's colour is refreshed on every hit, never left to drift while the fast path is being taken. The stale-colour outcome needs the opposite combination: a panel-level MISS whose (text,x,y) still equal the widget cache's recorded triple. A panel miss can only come from (a) a different text, (b) a different x/y - both of which are inside the widget fingerprint (SSR_Widgets.mqh:230-233), so Same() returns false anyway - (c) Exists()==false, in which case Same()'s own ObjectFind check (line 88) also returns false, or (d) ClearCache(), which is only ever paired with m_w.RemoveAll()/ForgetAll() (SSR_Panel.mqh:292, 310-312). The one remaining route, slot aliasing (slots 30/31/32 and 12/17 are reused across ids/branches), is closed by HideSheets() (SSR_Panel.mqh:1270, 1284-1340), which m_w.Remove()s - i.e. deletes and Forgets - every sheet object including st1/st2/st3/posmore/poshint/trlbl/setuprow at the top of each repaint, so no cross-branch widget-cache entry survives to be matched. No reachable stale colour; this is a hardening request (a public Invalidate seam), not a defect.

The premise is half true: CSSRPanel::Text() (SSR_Panel.mqh:194-199) does write OBJPROP_COLOR on a hit without telling the widget cache, so m_cn[] can hold a colour the object no longer has. But the stated trigger - "a second panel-level cache miss asks for the recorded colour with the recorded text and position" - is unreachable by construction, not merely by today's clear-them-together accident. A panel miss can only be caused by (a) text differing (then m_ct[k] != text and Same() returns false), (b) x or y differing (then fp differs, because Label folds x and y into the fingerprint at SSR_Widgets.mqh:232-233), (c) !m_w.Exists(id) (then Same()'s own ObjectFind at SSR_Widgets.mqh:88 returns false), or (d) slot out of [0,SSR_SLOTS) - and in case (d) the fast path is never taken for that id at all, so no divergence can have been created. Every miss therefore either differs in a fingerprinted field or fails the existence probe. The only remaining path is an independent reset of the panel cache, and ClearCache() is called exactly twice (ctor SSR_Panel.mqh:292, and Create() line 312 one line after m_w.RemoveAll()/ForgetAll()). The one object drawn with m_w.Label() outside Text() ("taglbl", SSR_Panel.mqh:1373) never takes the fast path either. The public Invalidate(id) suggestion is a reasonable hardening, but there is no defect and no latent state to reach without new code.

The divergence is unreachable, and not for the reason given. Two independent structural facts close it. (1) SSR_Panel.mqh:1284-1340 HideSheets() runs at the TOP OF EVERY REPAINT and ObjectDelete()s every sheet-owned id (st1..st7, poshint, trlbl, posmore, ses*, pp_*, pr/pl/pn rows...). Text()'s fast path requires m_w.Exists(id), which is false for all of those at draw time, so the direct OBJPROP_COLOR write never executes for any sheet label. (2) For the ids that DO survive a repaint (title/build/capinfo/clock/prog/spdlbl/spdval/spdmean/stbal/stflt/stopen/stfid/stspread, slots 0-6 and 50-55), the panel cache key (text, x, y) is a strict SUBSET of the widget fingerprint (x, y, col, size, fontlen) + text. A panel-cache MISS therefore implies text, x or y differs from the values recorded by the last Label() call, which in turn guarantees Same() returns false and the full six writes run. I also checked the one path that could break the subset property - two different ids sharing a panel slot (slots 30/31/32 are shared between poshint/posmore/trlbl and st1/st2/st3, slot 50 by five stbal call sites) - and every shared slot belongs exclusively to sheet ids killed by HideSheets, while every persistent id owns a unique slot. No stale semantic colour can be observed. The finder's own stated mechanism (ClearCache and RemoveAll always run together) is not what protects this.

votes.reason: The mechanism is exactly as coded. Slot() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:58-77) stops at the first free-OR-matching slot, Forget() (101-107) then guards on m_ck[k]==name and silently no-ops when the probe lands on a freed earlier slot, and Keep() (91-99) writes a second copy there; nothing but ForgetAll() (Attach/RemoveAll) ever reclaims the orphan. Home-slot collisions are certain at this load: hashing the panel's real names (SSRP_ prefix, ~264 of them in 512 slots) with the file's own FNV-1a gives 53 colliding home slots (e.g. SSRP_lines/SSRP_pn3, SSRP_riskval/SSRP_spdseg0, SSRP_hintrow/SSRP_palette), and the churn that supplies the freed earlier slot is real - HideSheets() Removes ~100 names and 6x SSR_POS_MAX row names at the top of every repaint, and SSR_Panel.mqh:1937-1940 Hides four status names unconditionally per frame. I could not refute the duplicate-slot leak.
votes.corrected_claim: Forget() can resolve to a free earlier slot in the probe chain and clear nothing, after which Keep() stores a duplicate and the off-home entry is orphaned for the life of the cache. Two parts of the finding are wrong, though. votes.reason: The arithmetic claim is right - Mix() (SSR_Widgets.mqh:135) is a mod-2^64 polynomial hash, and for the two lowest terms a collision needs no overflow at all: fp = ... + bg*1000003 + edge, so (bg+d, edge-d*1000003) collides for |d|<=16. But the described outcome - two ATTAINABLE states of one widget colliding - does not exist here. I brute-forced every palette: for each of SSR_THEME_RAIL (51 tokens), LIGHT (51) and DARK (35), over all ordered pairs, there is no (bg1,bg2) with |diff|<=16 whose matching (edge1,edge2) differs by exactly -diff*1000003. Zero exact two-term collisions in all three palettes. The only remaining collisions are the overflow ones, which require the full 64-bit difference to vanish - probability ~2^-64 per pair of states, and no call site can be shown to reach one. Label()'s fingerprint is additionally injective in practice (a nonzero colour difference is multiplied by M^2 while the size and font-length terms are bounded by ~16 and ~20, so they cannot cancel it). What survives is a documentation defect: the header's 'NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION' is true of the text half only, and the numeric half is a hash whose collision-freedom is unverified rather than structural. No defect in the shipped build.

The arithmetic is right and the documented invariant at SSR_Widgets.mqh:40-44 ("NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION") is false for the numeric half: Mix() is a * 1000003 + b, so Rect()'s fingerprint is a linear form with bg weighted M=1000003 and edge weighted 1. Since M < 2^24 and (long)color spans 0..0xFFFFFF, (bg+d, edge-d*M) for |d|<=16 collides without any overflow at all, and ButtonC's seven chained Mix calls (SSR_Widgets.mqh:364-365) put bg at M^3 ~ 1e18 where wraparound is genuine. Same() verifies nothing against the object beyond ObjectFind, so a collision would skip all nine writes. What keeps this from being a defect rather than a falsified comment: every colour argument in this codebase is a compile-time palette token (A17 enforces that no colour is written outside SSR_Theme.mqh), the value space is therefore a few dozen constants per role, and the finder states they could exhibit no colliding pair - I could not either. x, y, w and h are small ints whose weights (M^5..M^2) do not overlap their ranges. So the reachable-collision question cannot be settled from source without enumerating every (bg,edge,fg,size) combination actually drawn, and the real, provable content is the broken invariant plus the absence of read-back verification. Severity reduced from MEDIUM: no reachable collision was shown and the palette makes one unlikely.

votes.reason: Traced and it is worse than runtime-contingent - it is deterministic. The last M1 bar exists because a tick landed in it, so for a symbol that has stopped quoting the last quote necessarily satisfies lastbar_open <= last_quote <= lastbar_close, making the test at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:123 true and out.last_msc = lastbar_open-1, discarding a bar that can never receive another tick. The else branch is only taken when the last quote is NEWER than the final bar's close, i.e. when the M1 series is lagging the quote feed. The consumer chain is as claimed: SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1075 uses range.last_msc directly as win_end, and CSSRHistoryCatalog exposes the same range. No guard, clamp or later correction exists anywhere on that path.
votes.corrected_claim: Correct, and broader than the weekend case: the test fires for ANY last_quote at or before the final bar's close, which includes a stale quote that predates the last bar entirely (a symbol whose M1 was downloaded from the server while it is not being quoted). So the one-minute shortfall applies whenever quoting has stopped or lags the series, not only on a Saturday; the else branch that keeps the full last bar is taken only when the quote feed is ahead of the M1 series.

votes.reason: The arithmetic is exactly as described and checks out against the constants: SSR_MSC_PER_MIN is 60000 (SSR_Types.mqh:31), lastbar_close = lastbar_open + 59999, and the true branch sets out.last_msc = lastbar_open - 1, which drops the whole final M1 bar (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:117-125). The forming-bar proxy "last quote falls inside the last bar" is indeed unconditionally true on a closed market, because the tick that created the final bar IS the last quote, and the code tests neither SymbolInfoSessionQuote/SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE nor the lag against wall time. It stays POTENTIAL_RISK under this lens because the conclusion rests entirely on the runtime value SymbolInfoInteger(SYMBOL_TIME_MSC) returns for a closed symbol - plausibly the cached Friday quote (giving the off-by-one), but possibly 0 after a terminal restart or symbol re-select, which takes the else branch and is correct - and that cannot be settled without a terminal. Impact is bounded at one M1 bar on win_end (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1076 uses range.last_msc directly), so LOW is right.

The logic is exactly as described. SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:121-128 uses 'is the symbol's last quote inside the last bar?' as a proxy for 'is that bar still forming', and on a closed market the last quote is ALWAYS inside the last bar (the last bar is by definition the one the last tick built), so the test fires and out.last_msc = lastbar_open - 1 drops a bar that can never change again. No session-state check (SymbolInfoSessionQuote, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE) or wall-clock-lag check exists to separate the two cases. But the impact under any realistic use is one M1 bar at the far end of a timeline thousands of bars long, and it errs in the SAFE direction: it withholds data, it never exposes anything beyond the horizon, so no future-data or money-arithmetic consequence. The user-visible consequence is that LatestStart/CanStartAt/win_end land one minute earlier than they could - nothing they can perceive, and every downstream consumer stays self-consistent because they all read the same shortened bound. LOW overstates a one-minute conservative bias; this is a boundary-precision cleanup.

votes.reason: Every link in the chain checks out and I found no guard that breaks it. Discover()'s probe window is hardcoded to the newest 24h (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:135-139) and is the ONLY writer of out.has_ticks (grep confirms: the only other has_ticks assignment in production is the memory source). CSSRMt5DataSource copies it once (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:68) and Ticks() returns the provider whenever it is true (91-96), so the NULL-fallback at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:337-345 never fires. Load() sets SetTicksAvailable(range.has_ticks) (806), and Decide() only degrades FULL_TICK on !m_ticks_available (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:113-117). With a non-bulk pump, EmitWindow takes the FULL_TICK branch, ReadTicks returns 0 with Succeed() (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:428-430: got==0 -> break -> return total==0), n>0 gates both EmitTicks and PublishTicks, and the code does `emitted = n; m_cursor.Advance(hi, emitted, 0); return emitted;` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:365-368) - clock advances, nothing emitted, no warning. I grepped for any stall/zero-emit detector in Core and Data: none exists. CSSRMt5TickProvider::HasTicks(symbol, from, to) (line 379) genuinely has no production caller. The host's own diagnostic asserts the opposite (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2267-2271).
votes.corrected_claim: Correct as a trace; two qualifications. Category is wrong - nothing future-dated leaks; this is a range-blind capability probe producing a silent no-data replay plus a fidelity claim the run cannot honour. And the failure is not total: Decide() falls to SSR_FIDELITY_BAR on any bulk pump (owed_msc >= SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC, SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:119-123), so bars DO flow at high speed and after jumps while a 1x pump emits nothing - which makes the symptom intermittent and the misdiagnosis worse rather than better. Severity HIGH rather than CRITICAL: the session visibly fails to play instead of producing wrong results, and no trade or price data is corrupted.

votes.reason: Every link in the chain is in the source I read. Discover() decides a range-wide capability from a fixed probe over the newest 24 hours of history - from_msc = last_msc - 86400000, out.has_ticks = (got > 0) (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:132-138) - and nothing else ever sets it. CSSRMt5DataSource copies it into m_has_ticks (SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:68) and Ticks() returns the provider whenever it is true (91-96), so the engine's only degradation hook - `if(tp == NULL)` at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:337-345 - cannot fire; CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide degrades FULL_TICK solely on !m_ticks_available (SSR_FidelityPolicy.mqh:114-118), which Load set from range.has_ticks (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:806). The host requests FULL_TICK unconditionally on has_ticks (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153). With ReadTicks returning 0 for the older window, the FULL_TICK branch does `emitted = n; m_cursor.Advance(hi, emitted, 0); return emitted;` (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:366-368) and never reaches the bar path below, so no bar is emitted and no error is raised; I searched for a stall/no-emission watchdog and there is none (the only `stalls` counter is in the history-download loop, SSReplayStandalone.mq5:652-691). Old windows are fully supported inputs (InpStart is a free datetime at line 70, plus InpPickStart and random start), the range-aware HasTicks(symbol, from_msc, to_msc) at SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:379 has no caller anywhere, and the file's own header (lines 16-19) and SSR_Mt5DataSource.mqh:84-89 both describe precisely this failure. Severity reduced from CRITICAL to HIGH: the failure additionally requires the broker's tick base to be shallower than its M1 base over the chosen window, which is runtime/broker behaviour, and the outcome is a non-functioning replay rather than data corruption or a real order.

Confirmed end to end from source, and reachable on a headline feature. Discover() hardcodes the probe to [last_msc - 86400000, last_msc] (SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:135-139) and that single newest-day answer is the only thing that sets out.has_ticks. The panel prints the daily line only behind 'm_state.prop_daily_pct > 0.0' and otherwise renders T(SSR_S_NO_DAILY_LIMIT) (SSR_Panel.mqh:1788-1793), and the drawdown line likewise behind prop_total_pct (l.1805-1808); the port even documents this exact trap at SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:163-167 and QA stage 38 asserts it (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:4099-4121). Headline()'s 'floor %.2f' branch (l.319-321) is only reached while the state is RUNNING, and the panel draws prop_headline only when prop_state >= 2, i.e. PASSED/FAILED/VOID (SSR_Panel.mqh:1838-1841) - in which case Headline() returns the verdict branch at l.315-318, never the floor. out.prop_floor (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:214) has no reader at all: a full grep of MQL5/ finds it only in its declaration, its Init and that assignment. No statement, review card or log prints a floor either.

votes.reason: Provable. A full grep of MQL5/ finds exactly two OnClock fan-out sites, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1027-1029 (Pump) and 1102-1104 (PumpTo); JumpForward (l.1333-1419) does the bulk SeedBars, EmitWindow for the partial bar, m_sink.OnSeek, RepairWarmupIfLost, Publish and Transition(COMPLETED) with no observer OnClock loop and no CheckObserverPause. CSSRPropEvaluation overrides only OnClock/OnRewind/OnSessionStart, so the ticks EmitWindow publishes reach it not at all. JumpForward is user-reachable: JumpTo (l.1484-1519) is the 'unified entry point: the panel and the dialog both call this' and forwards to it. When the jump lands on the timeline end, m_clock.IsCompleted() transitions to COMPLETED, Pump early-returns 0 for any status != PLAYING (l.997-998), and Play() refuses outright after COMPLETED (l.971-976) - so no OnClock ever runs again and State() stays SSR_PROP_RUNNING, which the statement prints as 'IN PROGRESS' (SSR_Journal.mqh:286-297 via StateName(), SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:57). The per-pump rather than per-tick judging is also correct as described.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate for the jump-to-end case, with two refinements: (a) when the forward jump does NOT complete the replay, the next Pump's OnClock does judge - RollDay recomputes m_total_days from the new day index, so the deadline fires late rather than never; what is permanently lost is any breach or target reached inside the skipped span (equity is only sampled at the jump's end). (b) The 'review card' does not print the verdict - SSR_Review.mqh has no prop fields; the stuck 'IN PROGRESS' shows in the HTML statement (SSR_Journal.mqh:286-297) and the panel's prop sheet.

Pump/PumpTo both early-return 0 when status != PLAYING (l.997-998, 1071-1072), so once the jump lands on the timeline end and the clock completes, no OnClock ever fires again and the state stays SSR_PROP_RUNNING -> StateName() 'IN PROGRESS' in both Report() (used by the statement, SSR_Journal.mqh:295) and the panel. The secondary point is also accurate: even in normal play the rules are evaluated once per pump against end-of-pump equity, so an intra-pump breach that recovers is not seen.

Verified line by line: JumpForward (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1333-1419) does the bulk SeedBars, EmitWindow for the partial bar, m_sink.OnSeek, RepairWarmupIfLost, Publish and Transition(COMPLETED) - and contains no m_obs[i].OnClock loop, unlike Pump (l.1027-1029) and PumpTo (l.1102-1104); Pump returns 0 immediately when status != PLAYING (l.997-998). CSSRPropEvaluation overrides only OnSessionStart, OnClock, OnRewind and PauseRequested - no OnTicks - so OnClock is its sole judging point, yet the trading engine DOES process the emitted ticks, so stops fill and equity moves through the whole jumped span unjudged. JumpTo is the unified panel/dialog entry point (l.1482-1519), so this is a first-class control, not an edge path. I upgrade from LOW because the consequence is a dishonest verdict, not a cosmetic one: a jump that reaches the window end leaves the exported statement and review card printing 'IN PROGRESS' forever, and - worse - a daily-loss or drawdown breach that occurred inside the jumped span and had recovered by the next pump is never judged at all, so a run that should read FAILED can go on to read PASSED. votes.reason: Traced and provable. CSSRPropEvaluation has no SaveInto/RestoreFrom (grep of the file: none), and CSSRSessionManager writes only the streams, m_acct and m_stats (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:193-198) and restores only those (l.366-374); docs/audit/maps/ui-port-session.md:247-248 states outright 'Not stored: ... the prop evaluation'. Reset() (l.327-341) re-bases m_peak_eq/m_low_eq/m_day_open_eq on m_rules.start_balance, zeroes m_trading_days and m_total_days, and takes m_last_positions from the restored count; the first-clock branch (l.366-377) then overwrites m_peak_eq/m_day_open_eq with CURRENT equity and sets m_total_days = 1 and m_first_day to the resumed day. So with trailing rules the total floor rebases to 9400-1000 = 8400 instead of 10000-1000 = 9000, the deadline restarts at day 1 of 30, and the minimum-days count restarts at 0 - while the account and its equity curve ARE restored. The verdict genuinely differs from the same trades taken in one sitting, and it differs in the trader's favour.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate, with the sequencing worth stating: after a resume the evaluation is already SSR_PROP_VOID (see trading-analytics-1), so OnClock early-returns at l.360 and the re-basing only takes effect once the user presses Reset - which finding 1 forces them to do. Note also that the omission is a recorded design decision (docs/audit/maps/ui-port-session.md:247-248 'Not stored: ... the prop evaluation'), so this is an acknowledged gap rather than an accidental one; the wrong-verdict consequence is real either way.

votes.reason: Provable. Positions() returns m_acct.Total() (l.134-135) which is m_count (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:973), and Open() does 'int i = m_count++;' (l.719) BEFORE the pending branch (l.728-737), which returns with state SSR_POS_PENDING and no fill. Cancellation only sets m_pos[i].state = SSR_POS_CANCELLED (l.872) and never decrements m_count - the only m_count-- in the file is the immediate rollback for a pending with no price (l.732). OnClock (l.383-388) compares the count alone and never inspects state, so the next clock after a placement sets m_day_traded = true for the day then open. Three days of place-and-cancel therefore satisfy min_trading_days with zero fills, and a pending placed on day 1 and filled on day 2 credits day 1 - which contradicts the accessor's own comment at l.131-133 ('a trade was OPENED that day'). No QA stage covers it: the evaluation harness (SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5437-5452) only ever uses market Open/Close.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate. One reachability nuance: the count is only re-read inside OnClock, so an order placed and cancelled while the replay is PAUSED is attributed to whatever day is open at the next pump, not to the day it was placed.

Provable from source: Positions() returns m_acct.Total() (l.134-135) which is m_count (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:973), CSSRTradingEngine::Open() increments m_count and returns at the SSR_POS_PENDING branch before any fill (l.719-738), and Close() on a pending merely stamps SSR_POS_CANCELLED without decrementing m_count (l.868-876) - PendingCount/ClosedCount exist but the evaluation never consults state. So OnClock's `pos > m_last_positions` (l.383-388) does credit a trading day for a pending order that was placed and cancelled, and credits the placement day rather than the fill day - which contradicts the file's own comment at l.131-133 ('a trade was OPENED that day'). Impact is small and confined to a self-imposed training rule: min_trading_days can be satisfied without a fill, but gaming it takes deliberate effort across separate replay days, no money arithmetic is touched, and the header already states that firms differ on this definition and that it is an input. Host: g_prop.Reset() runs unconditionally after SetRules and Watch(GetPointer(g_prop)) runs when CfgProp() (SSReplayStandalone.mq5, the prop block around l.1184-1203), and Watch() is g_ctrl.AddObserver (l.869-877), so the evaluation is an observer of g_ctrl. g_ctrl is m_group's first stream (l.1320 g_group.Add(GetPointer(g_ctrl))). g_ctrl.Load (l.1252) fans OnSessionStart out to every observer (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:835-837), whose override calls Reset() (l.343-349) leaving m_state = SSR_PROP_RUNNING because enabled. Later, l.1483 g_session_mgr.Restore(CfgSession()) ends with 'At(i).NotifyRestored()' per stream (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:379-381) = PublishRewind(m_clock.now_msc) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1668-1669) = OnRewind on every observer (l.233-238). OnRewind's only guard is m_state != SSR_PROP_RUNNING (l.445-446), which does not hold, so the run goes VOID with m_pause_pending = true before a single candle plays, and the reason text asserts a backwards clock move that did not happen - the rewind is to 'now'. The pending pause is then consumed by CheckObserverPause at the end of the first Pump. Requires InpProp plus InpResume plus an existing session file, exactly as claimed.

The whole chain is in source and unconditional. Host: g_prop.SetRules/Reset() (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1195-1197) leaves m_state = SSR_PROP_RUNNING whenever rules.enabled, Watch(g_prop) adds it to g_ctrl's observer list (Watch at l.869-871 calls g_ctrl.AddObserver), g_ctrl is in g_group (l.1320), and g_ctrl.Load fires OnSessionStart -> Reset() again (RUNNING). Then Restore (l.1481-1486 when resuming) ends with 'for i: m_group.At(i).NotifyRestored()' (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:381-382) -> CSSRReplayController::NotifyRestored = PublishRewind(m_clock.now_msc) (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1668-1669) -> every observer's OnRewind (l.233-237). CSSRPropEvaluation::OnRewind guards only on enabled && state == RUNNING (l.445-446), so it flips to SSR_PROP_VOID and sets m_pause_pending, which CheckObserverPause consumes on the first pump. The reason string claims the clock moved backwards when the 'rewind' is to now_msc itself. No runtime assumption is involved - this is pure call-graph, and it disables the evaluation feature entirely for anyone who uses InpSession + InpResume.

The chain is fully verifiable. Host: g_prop.Reset() at :1197 (state -> RUNNING when CfgProp()), Watch(g_prop) at :1200 adds it to g_ctrl's observers (Watch -> g_ctrl.AddObserver, :869-877); g_ctrl.Load at :1252 publishes OnSessionStart to every observer (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:835-837), whose prop override calls Reset() again -> RUNNING; g_ctrl is in g_group (:1320); then :1483 g_session_mgr.Restore -> SSR_SessionManager.mqh:378-381 m_group.At(i).NotifyRestored() -> SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1668-1669 PublishRewind(m_clock.now_msc) -> l.233-238 calls OnRewind on every observer, and CSSRPropEvaluation::OnRewind (l.443-452) guards only on enabled && RUNNING, so it goes VOID with a reason text asserting the clock moved backwards when in fact it was published AT now.
