votes.reason: Confirmed by reading both paths in one file. Create()'s post-failure fallback (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:337-347) tests existence as SymbolInfoInteger(m_symbol, SYMBOL_DIGITS) > 0 && GetLastError()==0, which evaluates false for an existing whole-point instrument clone (digits==0) regardless of the error code, so the branch takes the hard Fail(SSR_ERR_INTERNAL, 'CustomSymbolCreate(...) failed') instead of adopting the leftover the comment at 332-336 says it exists to adopt. Adopt() 100 lines later documents this exact test as wrong and replaced it with SYMBOL_EXIST + SYMBOL_CUSTOM (comment 433-450, checks 452-464) - the author's own record that digits==0 instruments are real and that this misread killed the one-window handover on US30. The secondary observation is also correct: the fallback checks SSRIsReplaySymbol (a name pattern) and never SYMBOL_CUSTOM, so it is simultaneously stricter on digits and looser on ownership than Adopt. T3.7 exists (SSR_T3_CustomSymbol.mq5:415-441) and exercises this fallback, so it would only cover the intended behaviour on digits>0 instruments. Reaching the failure needs Destroy() to have left the symbol behind, which is runtime, but the logic error and its consequence are provable here.

The predicate at SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:338-339, `exists = (SymbolInfoInteger(m_symbol, SYMBOL_DIGITS) > 0 && GetLastError() == 0)`, is false for a symbol that exists with 0 digits: the first conjunct fails before the error check is even relevant. This is precisely the misreading the file documents as a bug 100 lines later (the Adopt() banner at 434-450: '<= 0 digits' treated as 'no such symbol', which 'on US30 rejected a symbol that was sitting right there'), and Adopt was fixed to SYMBOL_EXIST + SYMBOL_CUSTOM (453-464) while Create's fallback was not. So in Create the leftover-adopt recovery path is dead on any whole-point instrument: Destroy() fails to remove the leftover, CustomSymbolCreate refuses the existing name, exists evaluates false, and Fail(SSR_ERR_INTERNAL, 'CustomSymbolCreate(...) failed') propagates to the sink as SINK_FAILED (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:191-195). The finder's secondary point also holds: the fallback substitutes SSRIsReplaySymbol - a bare StringFind of the suffix (SSR_SymbolNaming.mqh:74-77) - for the SYMBOL_CUSTOM ownership test Adopt uses. Whether a given broker's index actually carries 0 digits, and whether Destroy fails, are runtime conditions, but the predicate is wrong from source regardless.
votes.corrected_claim: Correct on the defect, wrong on the coverage claim: T3.7 (SSR_T3_CustomSymbol.mq5:415-436) does not exercise this fallback on any instrument. Create() calls Destroy() first (line 318), and with no chart open the CustomSymbolDelete normally succeeds, so the second Create takes the ordinary create path and never reaches line 338. The fallback is uncovered everywhere, not just on digits>0 symbols.

votes.reason: The code path is exactly as described and I found no guard. CloseCharts() (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:505-522) walks every chart and closes on a pure ChartSymbol(id) == m_symbol match, with no id == ChartID() exclusion; it runs from Destroy() (549) which runs from the sink's Release() (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:384-390) and its destructor (72-74). I checked the ownership guard: m_own_symbol gates both, but SetOwnsSymbol is never called by the Expert (only by SSR_T6_History.mq5), so it stays true and Destroy() does run. OnDeinit's user-removed branch does ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2192) and then g_charts.CloseOwned(); g_ctrl.Release() (2201-2202), so the close loop genuinely executes after an asynchronous symbol switch on the host chart in one-window mode. Whether ChartSymbol(ChartID()) still reports the replay symbol at that instant, and whether the terminal honours ChartClose on the chart of an EA inside OnDeinit, are terminal behaviours not decidable from source - hence POTENTIAL_RISK, as the finder stated.

The source half is exactly as described: CloseCharts() walks ChartFirst/ChartNext and closes on a bare symbol match with no `id == ChartID()` exclusion (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:505-522), and it runs from Destroy() (549) which runs from Release() (SSR_CustomSymbolSink.mqh:383-391) and from the sink destructor (73-74) and from Create() (318). I also confirmed the call order and its gate: the whole block is inside `if(user_removed)` (Expert:2152-2154), so on REASON_REMOVE the EA does ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period) at 2194 and then g_ctrl.Release() at 2204, with the code's own comment at 2186 recording the switch as asynchronous. Whether ChartSymbol(ChartID()) reflects a queued symbol change at that instant, and whether ChartClose on one's own chart is honoured inside OnDeinit, are terminal behaviours that cannot be settled from source and that the author has never measured - so POTENTIAL_RISK, as the finder graded it. A cheap `if(id == ChartID()) continue;` would close the question without needing a terminal.

Path and absence of a guard both verified: CloseCharts matches purely on ChartSymbol(id)==m_symbol with no id==ChartID() exclusion (SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:505-522), and in one-window mode the EA IS on the replay chart (g_on_replay_chart, g_replay_chart = ChartID() at EA:1276), where OnDeinit does ChartSetSymbolPeriod(ChartID(), g_origin, _Period) - documented asynchronous at EA:2186 - and then g_ctrl.Release() -> CSSRCustomSymbolSink::Release (line 383-391, m_own_symbol defaults true) -> Destroy() -> CloseCharts(). If ChartSymbol() has not yet caught up, ChartClose(ChartID()) is issued against the host window. I keep MEDIUM rather than downgrading because user_removed also covers REASON_CLOSE (EA:2152-2153): during terminal shutdown a closed chart is dropped from the saved profile, so the user's window and its template/objects do not come back next launch - more than cosmetic. It stays POTENTIAL_RISK because whether ChartSymbol reflects a pending ChartSetSymbolPeriod synchronously is terminal behaviour not decidable from source, and because the same race decides whether the symbol delete would have succeeded at all. No money, trade or history correctness is touched either way.
votes.corrected_claim: CloseCharts() has no id==ChartID() exclusion, so in one-window teardown (EA:2191-2204) it can ChartClose the EA's own window if the asynchronous switch back to the origin has not landed yet. Worst case is the loss of the user's chart window - permanently, when the reason is terminal close and the profile is saved without it - not any data or accounting error; the outcome depends on ChartSymbol()'s synchrony, which is unmeasured. Skipping ChartID() in the loop (and letting the EA's own chart return to the origin) is the fix.

votes.reason: Verified as stated and correctly self-limited. Html() (356-364) performs exactly four StringReplace calls under a comment asserting five; the apostrophe is absent, and & is replaced first so adding ' is safe. I checked every attribute the writer emits: all are double-quoted (class=, style=, title=), the only interpolated attribute is title="%s" at 570-574 fed by SSRFormatMsc (digits, dots, colons), and grep for =' across the Report layer finds only a JavaScript string comparison in SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:152 - no single-quoted HTML attribute exists. SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:23 is literally "<title>" + title + "</title>" with no escaping, and both call sites (SSR_ClassReport.mqh:447, SSR_Journal.mqh:264) pass string literals. So: a documented-versus-implemented mismatch plus a latent escaping hole in shared code, with no current exploit path - exactly the IMPROVEMENT the finder claimed.

The reading of the code is accurate (four StringReplace calls under a comment claiming five; SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:23 splices `title` into <title> unescaped), but there is no reachable defect. Every attribute Write() emits is double-quoted, and I checked each Html() sink in this file - lines 521, 561, 618, 650 and 652 are all element text content, where an apostrophe needs no escaping per HTML parsing rules. The one interpolated attribute, title="%s" at 571, is fed SSRFormatMsc (digits, dots, colons and spaces only), and both SSRWriteReportHead call sites pass string literals. So this is a comment/code mismatch and a hardening suggestion, not a defect - which the finding itself concedes.

votes.reason: Group() does return an un-refused, half-built shift-0 group, but only on a narrower precondition than the finder describes, and more fields are wrong than claimed. Trace: crossing into an older group hits the early `if(seen == shift && open_set) return true;` at 104-105, so a complete group is returned there. Line 136 is reached only when the backward walk never leaves group 0 - i.e. EVERY bar in the buffer belongs to the requested shift-0 group. In that case out.open was last overwritten at 125 from m_m1[0] (the oldest bar the buffer happens to hold), the shift==0 branch returns true, and neither m_refusals++ nor the false that the shift>0 case gets is executed. Available() returns 1 for that single group (372), so an availability check does not protect a caller. Reachable: early in a bar-driven session (OnSessionStart zeroes m_count, the first pump publishes a handful of M1 bars), or right after session start where PrimeView clamps `from` to StartMsc (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:396-397), or after a deep OnRewind - any moment when the whole buffer fits inside one H1/H4/D1 group.
votes.corrected_claim: Same defect, two corrections. (1) The trigger is not merely "the group began before the buffer did" and it is not reachable via MakeRoom: MakeRoom keeps 2048 M1 bars (~34 hours), which always spans several H4 groups, so the early-return at line 104 fires first. It needs the entire buffer to lie inside the requested shift-0 group, which happens early in a session or just after a rewind that trimmed almost everything. (2) high and low are NOT right either - they are folded only over the minutes present in the buffer, so the group's true extreme can be in the missing earlier part. Only close is certainly correct. out.spread being the newest minute's value (copied once at line 110) is arguably the intended reading of a forming bar's spread rather than a defect.

votes.corrected_claim: Real, but the trigger in the claim is wrong. The state needs the ENTIRE buffer inside one tf group, which for H4 (240 M1 bars) means fewer than 240 buffered bars - i.e. the first minutes of a session, where PrimeView clamps `from` to g_ctrl.StartMsc() (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:395-397) so the pre-window part of the H4 group can never be in the buffer. votes.reason: The asymmetry is real and provable. When the backward walk exhausts the buffer while still inside group 0, the post-loop block at 132-138 returns true for shift 0 while shift>0 gets m_refusals++ and false, and out.open was last written at line 125 from m_m1[0] - the oldest bar the buffer happens to hold, not the group's first M1 bar. The shipped reference strategy is protected twice over (it requires Available(tf) >= lookback+2 and reads shifts 1 and 2), so nothing in the product observes it today.

votes.reason: The starvation path is provable. CSSRMarketView's only bar inputs are OnBarContext and Prime; grep shows OnBarContext has exactly one caller (PublishBar, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:191-196) and PublishBar exactly one call site (506), inside the bar-driven section that the FULL_TICK branch has already returned from at line 369 (it calls PublishTicks at 366 and returns). Prime has exactly one caller, PrimeView (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:403), which OnTimer gates on `g_view.M1Count() == 0` (2797) - false forever after the first successful prime, since nothing resets m_count except OnSessionStart or a rewind that trims everything. Meanwhile OnTicks (191-198) and OnClock (200-201) keep m_bid/m_ask/m_now_msc live, so Now()/Bid()/Ask() advance while every bar accessor is frozen, and Available() keeps reporting the frozen groups, so the strategy cannot detect it. SSR_RefStrategy.mqh:96-128 does exactly what the claim says: Bar(m_tf,1), HighestHigh/LowestLow(m_tf,2,lookback), then compares sl against ctx.market.Bid()/Ask(). FULL_TICK is selected whenever the scanned range has tick history (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1153) and the pump does not hit the bulk threshold.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate except for "no OnBarContext for the whole session": any pump owing >= SSR_BULK_THRESHOLD_MSC (10 minutes, e.g. after a real timer stall) degrades to SSR_FIDELITY_BAR in CSSRFidelityPolicy::Decide and does take the bar-driven path, publishing bars and refreshing the view. In steady FULL_TICK playback, which is the normal case, no bar is ever published and the view stays frozen at the first prime, so the defect stands; it is also gated on InpRefStrategy (default false) plus broker tick history existing for the symbol.

prev_close/prev_was_loss are assigned unconditionally at the end of every kept slot (l.511-512) and the walk is m_acct.At(i) in slot order, so 'previous' is the previously-created trade, not the most recent close before this open - the finder's A/B/C case misses a textbook revenge entry. votes.reason: ClosedDrawdownFor (SSR_Statistics.mqh:694-717) accumulates `bal += p.profit + p.swap - p.commission` while walking i=0..total-1 through m_acct.At(i, p), and At() is a straight slot read (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1004-1011) with slots appended in Open() order (l.719) and never sorted or compacted - I grepped the engine for ArraySort/ArrayRemove/compaction and there is none. MEDIUM is fair: a user-visible metric is wrong under ordinary multi-position use, with no guard.

ClosedDrawdownFor (SSR_Statistics.mqh:697-719) accumulates bal in At(i) order, which is creation/open order (m_pos append-only, SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:719; At :1005; nothing sorts by close_msc anywhere in the engine - I grepped for ArraySort/compaction and found none). A replay that only revealed a release once the clock reached it would be teaching the opposite of the skill: a real trader knows the calendar days ahead, and deciding not to be in a trade at 15:30 is most of what the calendar is for.' Lines 16-18 then name the single exception and who enforces it, matching the host's blind-mode refusal at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:923-928 that the finding cites as evidence of an unapplied principle — the principle WAS applied, to the one mode where an event name leaks the hidden instrument and date. A scheduled release time is public information a real trader has in advance; it is not price information the replay has not reached, so no 'now-bounded accessor' is missing from CSSRCalendar. The code traces exactly as described (Load with the full window, At(0..Count-1), one OBJ_VLINE per item) but the described outcome is the documented intent, not a defect.

The behaviour is an explicit, documented design decision, not an omission. SSR_CalendarLines.mqh:10-14 states it in capitals: "THE FUTURE IS DRAWN ON PURPOSE. A replay that only revealed a release once the clock reached it would be teaching the opposite of the skill: a real trader knows the calendar days ahead, and deciding not to be in a trade at 15:30 is most of what the calendar is for." Lines 16-18 name the one exception and the finding's own cited counter-example is that exception being enforced: "BLIND MODE IS THE EXCEPTION and the host enforces it", which the host does at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:925-929. The host comment at 906-919 repeats it ("Loaded once, drawn once"). So the absence of a now-bounded accessor on CSSRCalendar is intentional, and the finder's premise — that showing an upcoming release "is the one thing a market-replay trainer must not show" — is contradicted by the design the file states. The finder also concedes on-screen visibility is unverifiable.

votes.reason: The probe at line 245 is CalendarValueHistory(probe, from, to) with NO country_code and NO currency argument — unlike Pull, which passes a currency (line 137) — and no importance filter, so it asks for every event of every country in the window. `from`/`to` are the caller's window widened by 86400 s at each end (lines 217-218), so the probe always spans at least ~2 full days plus the window; the 2024.12.25 example resolves to 2024.12.24..2024.12.26. A terminal with a working calendar returning zero events worldwide across such a span is not a reachable state, which is precisely why the crude count works as a discriminator: the author deliberately widened the question (all countries, all importances) rather than reusing the filtered query. The misleading note the finding describes therefore exists as a code path but has no reachable input on a terminal whose calendar is present. The suggested alternatives are a style preference, not a fix for a reachable defect.

The logical gap is real and visible in source: the comment at SSR_Calendar.mqh:239-242 sets out to distinguish "no calendar" from "a quiet week", and line 245-246 then uses the event count over the same widened window as the discriminator, so zero events is reported as "this terminal returned no calendar at all ... This is not the same as a quiet week." (250-255), which is precisely the confusion it set out to avoid. GetLastError() is only quoted into the message, never tested. But reachability cannot be settled here: `CalendarValueHistory(probe, from, to)` with no country/currency filter is the unfiltered superset over a span of at least ~2 days across every country, and whether that is ever empty on a working terminal is broker/terminal data I cannot verify — which is exactly why this is at most POTENTIAL_RISK. Impact is also bounded: because the probe is a superset of the filtered Pulls, `any == 0` implies `m_count == 0`, so nothing is lost but the wording of the note (printed at SSReplayStandalone.mq5:948-949).
votes.corrected_claim: The probe conflates "no calendar facility" with "no events in this window", and the resulting note asserts "This is not the same as a quiet week" when it may be exactly that. The finder's scenario (a 2-hour Christmas window widened to three days) is the least likely trigger, since the probe is unfiltered across all currencies; the plausible trigger is a replay window outside the terminal's downloaded calendar coverage (e.g. pre-2008 history). Impact is confined to the diagnostic string: the probe is a superset of the filtered pulls, so a false 'no calendar' verdict can only occur when m_count was already 0.

votes.reason: Traced end to end and every cited fact holds. SetSlot (line 121) takes any int with no clamp and no error path; SSRGvName (SSR_Contract.mqh:124-127) concatenates whatever it is given; CSSRClient::Discover scans only 1..SSR_MAX_SLOTS with SSR_MAX_SLOTS 8 (SSR_Client.mqh:64, SSR_Contract.mqh:156); the host assigns extra streams InpSlot+1+i (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1396, and the custom-symbol sink the same way at :490); InpSlot is an unvalidated input (:74) copied into the session file (:422) and never range-checked anywhere in the tree. Begin() (lines 134-147) writes the slot's variables unconditionally, with no check for a live heartbeat already on that slot, so overlapping slots silently share one namespace — exactly what SSR_Contract.mqh:47-49 says slots exist to prevent.
votes.corrected_claim: Two corrections to the magnitudes. (1) Extra streams are capped at SSR_EXTRA_STREAMS = SSR_MAX_STREAMS - 1 = 3 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:255, SSR_MasterClock.mqh:34), so the highest slot a session can ever occupy is InpSlot+3 and a stream only becomes undiscoverable when InpSlot >= 6, not merely at InpSlot=8. (2) The second-session collision is partially detected, not entirely silent: the host scans existing replay symbols for its own '.SSR<slot>' suffix and prints '[host] NOTE: <sym> is OPEN and also on replay slot N ... set Replay slot to N+1 on one of them' (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1604-1628), which fires when a second session's primary slot collides with an earlier session's extra-stream slot. It is a Print, not a refusal, and it covers only the custom-symbol namespace — nothing checks the publisher's global-variable namespace or an existing heartbeat, so the finding's core point stands.

votes.reason: Trace confirms no cache and no header-only mode anywhere on the path. SessionSummary (GroupPort:932-940) calls m_sessions.Peek, which constructs a local CSSRSessionFile and calls f.Load(Path(name)) (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:215-219); Load (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:206-259) reads the file line by line to EOF, growing m_ent_sec/m_ent_key/m_ent_val for every entry - pos, leg and e rows included - before Peek reads its five keys. The dialog calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) inside the row loop for SSR_SD_ROWS=8 (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:27, 157-178), and Render() runs from Open() and from the up, down, row, load and del handlers (255, 257, 262-268, 284, 293). Severity stays LOW: it is a modal, user-paced interaction and the cost is a file parse per visible row per click, not a correctness fault.

Mechanism verified end to end. CSSRSessionManager::Peek (SessionManager:216-243) constructs a local CSSRSessionFile and calls f.Load(Path(name)); Load (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:206-259) reads the file line by line to EOF, appending every key=value pair - including every pos/leg/e row - into the dynamic m_ent_sec/m_ent_key/m_ent_val arrays before Peek reads its five [session] keys. GroupPort::SessionSummary (l.932-940) calls Peek per index with no cache, and the dialog calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) inside its row loop bounded by SSR_SD_ROWS = 8 (SessionDialog:27, 172-173), with Render() re-entered on up, down, row click, load and after save (SessionDialog:255-257, 264, 284, and Open() from RequestSave). There is no header-only read mode anywhere. Two corrections to the magnitude rather than the mechanism: the parse is bounded by SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES = 16384 and SSR_SF_MAX_SECTIONS = 1024 (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:33-34), so the worst case is ~16k entries per file and ~131k per render, not the unbounded 9,000-per-file figure implied; and the cost is string/array work in a modal that a human clicks a handful of times, so it is an efficiency wart, not a hang. Severity stays LOW.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate: Peek fully parses each session file and the dialog calls it once per visible row on every Render(), with no cache and no header-only mode. The per-file parse is capped by SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES = 16384 / SSR_SF_MAX_SECTIONS = 1024, so the worst case is roughly 8 x 16k entries per click rather than an unbounded amount.

votes.reason: The mechanism is real: Peek constructs a CSSRSessionFile and calls Load (SSR_SessionManager.mqh:213-219), which parses every line of the file into three parallel dynamic arrays before a single key is read (SSR_SessionFile.mqh:206-258), and the dialog calls m_port.SessionSummary(idx) once per visible row inside its render loop with SSR_SD_ROWS = 8 (SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:27, 172-174). No cache, no header-only mode. But the cost is far smaller than claimed and the trigger is narrower. votes.reason: The truncation is plainly in the source. SSRFlightSample.chart_id is a long (SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:58), filled from g_charts.IdAt(0) at Standalone.mq5:2408-2409, and Write formats it as (int)s.chart_id against a %d specifier (SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:243, 256), so any id above 2^31-1 is written wrapped and often negative into the chart_id column of the diagnostic artefact. The finding is honest that "real chart ids exceed 2^31" is an inference about MT5's id scheme rather than evidence from this tree - but the cast is lossy for such ids regardless, and the fix (%I64d or IntegerToString) needs no runtime knowledge. The same (int) cast is applied to emit_calls/emit_ticks/seed_bars/truncations at 254-255.
votes.corrected_claim: Confirmed for chart_id. The emit_ticks/emit_calls half is far weaker: those would need to exceed 2.1 billion in one recording (over 268 million bars at the default 8 ticks/bar) before wrapping, so in practice chart_id is the only column that truncates.

votes.reason: The cast is real and lossy: FlightRecorder:256 passes (int)s.chart_id into a %d slot of the sample row, and s.chart_id is filled from g_charts.IdAt(0), a long chart id (Standalone:2407-2409). MQL5's StringFormat %d takes a 32-bit argument, so a long id has to be widened to %I64d or routed through IntegerToString rather than truncated; C-style truncation of a value above 2^31 yields a wrong and frequently negative number in the one column that says which window a fault occurred on, in the artefact the author depends on for remote diagnosis. The one thing I cannot settle from this tree is the magnitude of real MT5 chart ids - that comes from MT5's time-derived id scheme, not from source - but the cast is unconditionally lossy above 2^31 whatever the distribution, and no other code in the tree ever narrows a chart id this way. I do refute the extension of the claim to the instrumentation counters: (int)s.emit_ticks and (int)s.emit_calls would need 2^31 ticks in one recording (at 8 ticks per bar that is ~268M bars), which SSR_FLIGHT_MAX_ROWS-capped sessions cannot plausibly reach, so those casts are not a live defect. Severity LOW: a diagnostic column, not behaviour.

The same-cast claim for emit_ticks/emit_calls does not hold - reaching 2^31 emitted ticks in a single capped recording is not achievable in practice.

votes.reason: Traced end to end and every link holds. RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3093-3106) is the ONLY caller of g_dialog.Open(); it seeds r.start_msc = g_group.Now(), r.end_msc = g_group.EndMsc(). Because start_msc > 0 the catalogue-default branch in Open() (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:105-110) is skipped, so the user's typed start is validated only by SSRValidateRange (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:135), which measures against cat.EarliestStart(warm) and cat.LastMsc() (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:82-87) - the BROKER's M1 range, with no knowledge of the loaded replay window. CanStart() (:139-143) therefore returns true for any broker-servable date, 'start' sets m_confirmed and calls Close() (:313-318), and only then does RouteEvent check `if(r.start_msc >= g_group.StartMsc() && r.start_msc < g_group.EndMsc())` else Print(...) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3181-3192). Close() has already destroyed every object (:115-122), so no surface remains to report the refusal; the user gets a closed dialog and an Experts-log line. Title is literally "NEW SESSION" and the button "START" (SSR_Strings.mqh:517-518), reinforcing the wrong expectation. No guard, clamp or earlier check anywhere narrows the accepted set to the loaded window.

Verified end to end. CSSRRangeDialog::CanStart (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:139-143) gates only on m_req.IsComplete(), m_quote.IsFeasible() and m_problem, and m_problem comes from SSRValidateRange (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:135), which measures exclusively against cat.EarliestStart(warm) and cat.LastMsc() (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:78-92) - the broker's M1 catalogue, never the loaded window. The only caller is RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3095-3106) and the only consumer of the confirmed request is SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3181-3192, which jumps only when r.start_msc is in [g_group.StartMsc(), g_group.EndMsc()) and otherwise only Prints. OnEvent calls Close() (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:313-318) before the host sees the request, and Close() does m_w.RemoveAll() + ChartRedraw, so every object that could carry a refusal is already gone. No guard, no alternative surface: a broker-servable but session-external date is accepted, closes the dialog, and produces nothing visible.

Verified end to end. SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:135 validates only against the catalogue (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:76-90 measures cat.EarliestStart/cat.LastMsc), and CanStart (:139-143) therefore enables START for any broker-servable instant. The sole caller is RunHostCommand(SSR_CMD_JUMP) (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3095-3107) and the confirm handler (:3181-3192) acts only when r.start_msc is inside [g_group.StartMsc(), g_group.EndMsc()); otherwise it Prints to the Experts log. Close() at :316 has already removed every dialog object, so no surface remains for feedback. Reachability is high rather than incidental: the dialog itself prints the BROKER's full range on the 'avail' label (:175-180) as the guide the user types against, so an out-of-window date is the natural thing to enter, and the title 'NEW SESSION' plus the button 'START' promise a reload the host cannot perform. Observable result is a primary command (J) that silently does nothing. No money arithmetic, no future-data exposure, no weakening of the virtual-trading guarantee, so MEDIUM is the ceiling - it is a silent no-op on a reachable path, not corruption.

votes.reason: Length arithmetic verified from source. SSR_SessionRange.mqh:84-85 builds StringFormat("start too early - %s context needs history back to %s", EnumToString(r.max_tf), SSRFormatMsc(earliest)). Literal part = 18 + 31 = 49 chars, EnumToString(PERIOD_D1) = 9, SSRFormatMsc returns TimeToString(TIME_DATE|TIME_MINUTES|TIME_SECONDS) = 19 chars (SSR_Time.mqh:61-67), total 77 (78 with PERIOD_M15). The value reaches OBJPROP_TEXT completely unguarded: CSSRRangeDialog::Render passes m_problem straight to m_w.Label (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:234) and CSSRWidgets::Label (SSR_Widgets.mqh:226-252) performs no Clip/StringSubstr - it writes ObjectSetString(OBJPROP_TEXT, text) verbatim. Cut at 63 the drawn string ends "...history back to 2019." exactly as claimed (49+9 = 58 chars of prose, then 5 date chars). Note the same label also carries "not enough history: " + q.ToString() (SSR_SessionRange.mqh:92), which is a second uncapped path into the same 63-char label. Contrast is real: the panel does Clip(...,62) elsewhere (SSR_Panel.mqh:1890) but this dialog does not.

Provable from source with the 63-char OBJPROP_TEXT ground truth. SSR_SessionRange.mqh:81-83 builds StringFormat("start too early - %s context needs history back to %s", EnumToString(r.max_tf), SSRFormatMsc(earliest)); the literal minus the two %s is 49 characters, EnumToString of the four offered timeframes (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:47-57) is 9-10 ("PERIOD_D1"/"PERIOD_M15"), and SSRFormatMsc uses TIME_DATE|TIME_MINUTES|TIME_SECONDS (SSR_Time.mqh:62-67) = 19 characters. So 77 (D1) to 78 (M15) characters go into one OBJ_LABEL. CSSRWidgets::Label (SSR_Widgets.mqh:226-252) writes OBJPROP_TEXT verbatim with no Clip/StringSubstr guard, unlike the panel's own Clip(...,62) usage (SSR_Panel.mqh:1893). The truncation falls inside the timestamp, so the only actionable part of the refusal is the part that is cut.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate, with two corrections: the literal part is 49 characters (not 48), giving 77 for PERIOD_D1 and 78 for PERIOD_M15; and the cut is not the only display problem - the dialog is SSR_DLG_W = 248 px wide (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:25) and the label is drawn at x+SSR_PAD with no width budget, so even a 63-character string overruns the dialog box.

Recompute() opens with `m_problem = "";` (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:127) and closes with `m_problem = SSRValidateRange(m_req, m_cat);` (:135) - the only early return is the m_cat == NULL branch (:129-133), and in both call sites m_cat is non-NULL (the 'more' branch is itself inside `if(m_cat != NULL)`). ENDEDIT path: `m_problem = "could not read that date..."` (:274) then Recompute() (:275) overwrites it, and because m_req.start_msc was NOT updated the verdict is recomputed on the unchanged previous instant, so CanStart() (:141) still returns true. The typed text also survives: Render() sets OBJPROP_TEXT on the edit box only inside `if(ObjectFind(...) < 0)` (:186-196), so the field keeps "march 5" while the engine holds the old date. LOAD MORE path: m_problem = "gained %d more bars" / "the broker has nothing older" (:304-306) is discarded by Recompute() on :307. Render() draws only m_problem into the sole 'problem' label (:233-234); there is no toast and no Print in this file, so both messages are unreachable by any channel. Events do arrive here - the dialog is created on g_panel_chart = ChartID(), the EA's own chart (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1463-1465), so ENDEDIT is genuinely delivered.

Straight dead-store, provable from source. Recompute() opens with m_problem = "" (SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:127) and ends by reassigning m_problem = SSRValidateRange(...) (:135). Both writers assign m_problem and then call Recompute() on the next statement: the ENDEDIT branch at :271-275 ('could not read that date...' then Recompute()) and the LOAD MORE branch at :303-307 ('gained %d more bars'/'the broker has nothing older' then Recompute()). Render() draws only m_problem into the single 'problem' label (:233-234), and the dialog has no other channel (no Print, no toast). The typo also survives on screen because Render() sets OBJPROP_TEXT on the OBJ_EDIT only inside the ObjectFind(...) < 0 creation branch (:186-196), so the unparsed text stays in the box while m_req.start_msc keeps the previous instant and CanStart() stays true - exactly the silent-failure the :270 comment claims to prevent.

Provable dead-store on both paths. Recompute() opens with m_problem = "" (:127) and closes by overwriting it with SSRValidateRange (:135), and both callers assign m_problem immediately before calling it: the ENDEDIT typo message (:274 then :275) and LOAD MORE's result (:304-306 then :307). Render() draws only m_problem into the 'problem' label (:234) and there is no other channel - no toast, no Print. The typo case is worse than a lost message because the OBJ_EDIT text is set only inside the creation branch (:186-196), so Render() never rewrites it: the box keeps 'march 5' while m_req.start_msc silently still holds the previous instant, START stays enabled, and pressing it commits a date the user never asked for. That is silent substitution of user input on a reachable path, which is exactly what the comment at :270 claims to prevent. votes.reason: Straight contradiction between two lists, both read. SSR_Strings.mqh:499-500 defines SSR_S_KEYS_2 = "+ - speed    R reset    J jump    B bookmark", drawn as the 'keyhint' label on the Session tab (SSR_Panel.mqh:1899-1901, inside the SSR_S_GRP_KEYBOARD group). The binding table says otherwise: SSRKeyBindings adds SSR_VK_R -> SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE ("stop and target lines on / off") in the TRADING block, and SSR_VK_0 -> SSR_CMD_RESET ("start the session over (asks first)") under a comment block headed "RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter" (SSR_Keys.mqh). SSRKeyToCommand is a pure table lookup, so pressing R genuinely toggles the lines and 0 is the only reset key - and "0" appears in none of the four SSR_S_KEYS_* strings, which are the panel's only keyboard guide. keys.3 even prints "L lines" for the same command, so the panel contradicts itself. The Persian catalogue faithfully reproduces the error: MQL5/Files/SSReplay/lang/fa.txt:216 reads `keys.2 = + - سرعت    R شروع دوباره    J پرش    B نشانه` ("R start over"). Nothing cross-checks these hand-written strings against SSRKeyBindings().

The mismatch is provable. SSR_Strings.mqh:499-500 sets SSR_S_KEYS_2 to "+ - speed    R reset    J jump    B bookmark" and SSR_Panel.mqh:1902-1904 draws it as the 'keyhint' label on the Session tab. SSR_Keys.mqh:162-164 binds SSR_VK_R to SSR_CMD_LINES_TOGGLE ('stop and target lines on / off') and SSR_Keys.mqh:200-202 binds SSR_CMD_RESET to SSR_VK_0, under a comment block ('RESET MOVED OFF R, and off every letter') that documents the move the hint line was never updated for. Nothing cross-checks these hand-written strings against SSRKeyBindings(). Downgraded to LOW rather than MEDIUM because the consequence is non-destructive in the safe direction - pressing R places the SL/TP lines instead of destroying the session - and the generated key card (H) still lists 0 correctly, so the correct information is reachable in the product.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate, with the impact stated more precisely: the wrong hint fails safe (R draws lines, it does not reset), and the authoritative list is still correct because SSR_KeyCard is generated from SSRKeyBindings(); the defect is that the panel's hand-written hint line contradicts it and fa.txt has translated the error.

votes.reason: Source supports the measurement-validity claim. Lines 93-103 issue exactly one CopyTicksRange over a fixed seven-day window (from = now - 7*86400 .. now, COPY_TICKS_ALL), assign the return straight to `cap`, and publish it as "copyticksrange_week_return" with the note "sets the page size for TickSource" under the comment "practical ceiling of one CopyTicksRange call". There is no second call over a wider window, no comparison against a known tick count, no GetLastError() check and no truncation test of any kind, so the code provably cannot distinguish 'the API refused to return more' from 'that is how many ticks the week held' - a quiet symbol yields a small number and a busy one a large number for reasons unrelated to any limit. The -1 error return is also published verbatim as a tick count. The cost observation holds too: a full week of COPY_TICKS_ALL per symbol for up to InpMaxAuto=6 symbols, in a file whose own comment at 60-64 says a single day of ticks per probe made the audit look hung. Severity LOW: a mislabelled metric in a spike/audit script that produces a report for a human, with no code consuming the value.

The semantics are as the finding states: CopyTicksRange returns the number of ticks it copied for the requested range (or -1 on error), not a per-call limit. SSR_B4_BrokerDataAudit.mq5:93-103 makes exactly one COPY_TICKS_ALL call over a fixed seven-day window, assigns the return straight to cap with no second call over a wider range, no comparison against a known count, and no GetLastError()/negative check - so a -1 error would be published as a tick figure too. The value is then labelled 'practical ceiling of one CopyTicksRange call' and noted as 'sets the page size for TickSource', neither of which the measurement can support: for any symbol whose week of ticks is below whatever real limit exists, cap is pure tick density. Severity LOW because this is spike tooling, not shipped code, but the conclusion it feeds (TickSource page size) is exactly the kind of decision the mislabel would corrupt.

votes.reason: The mechanism is provable and I could not find a guard that prevents it. CSSRBarProvider::NextBarOpen (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:150-165) calls the virtual ReadBars with from = after_msc + 1 for all four spans. CSSRMemoryBarProvider::ReadBars (Sources/SSR_MemoryDataSource.mqh:113-125) calls GuardRange first and returns 0 when it is false; GuardRange forwards to CSSRFutureGuard::ClampRange, which does `if(from_msc > m_horizon_msc) { Violation(from_msc); return false; }`. The callers do pass after_msc == now: CSSRReplayController::StepBars calls NextTimelineBarOpen(m_clock.now_msc) at line 1166 BEFORE m_guard.SetHorizon(m_clock.now_msc) at 1175, and the horizon is already == now from the previous pump/step (SetHorizon at 1009/1084/1175/1244/1361) or == timeline.start_msc at READY (Arm at 832). So from = now + 1 > horizon for all four spans: four Violation() increments and SSR_INVALID_TIME every time, whether or not there is a gap. The guard does reach this provider - the generic CSSRDataSource::SetGuard (SSR_IDataSource.mqh:244-253) is invoked from the controller at line 573. Two corrections below.

votes.reason: The finding misreads both the comment and the file. The comment's stated failure mode is 'a balance a cent short', i.e. 0.01, and CheckNear's predicate MathAbs(e-a) <= 0.005 (line 50) FAILS on a one-cent discrepancy - so the guarantee the prose actually names is provided, strictly and with margin. The title's claim that 'its CheckExact helper sits unused' is false: CheckExact is defined at line 47 and used at line 119. The tolerances in this file are chosen deliberately against the file format's stored precision - the adjacent comment at lines 427-428 reads 'the curve is stored to the cent, so two cents of tolerance is the honest bound, not a fudge' - and T12.4's own comment (lines 353-355) states the balance is REPLAYED from the position log rather than restored verbatim, so bit-equality on a sum of two-decimal leg amounts is not the correct assertion. What remains is the single word 'exactly' in a comment, with no code defect and no unguarded failure mode behind it.

The semantics of the serialization make exact equality unattainable and make 0.005 the correct bound, and the concrete guarantee the prose names IS enforced. CSSRTradingEngine::SaveInto writes balance_initial/balance_check with f.SetDouble(...,2) (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1048-1049) and each position's profit/swap/commission with DoubleToString(...,6) (1097-1099); RestoreFrom does NOT read the balance back - it replays it as m_balance += profit + swap - commission (1223) from those 6-decimal round-tripped values. A CheckExact (bit equality) on back.Balance() is therefore an assertion that cannot hold in general and would be flaky by construction. The failure the comment names - 'a balance a cent short' - is 0.01, which exceeds the 0.005 tolerance and FAILS the check; the engine's own disagreement warning uses the same order of magnitude (MathAbs(want-m_balance) > 0.01 at line 1258). 'Exactly' is loose prose for 'to the cent', not a stronger assertion the code fails to make.
votes.corrected_claim: At most a comment-wording nit: CheckNear(..., 0.005) is the tightest bound the 6-decimal position serialization permits and it does catch a one-cent discrepancy; the header's word 'exactly' should read 'to the cent'.

votes.reason: The named failure mode is caught. The header's words are 'a balance a cent short after a save is a bug nobody finds for months', and 0.01 > 0.005, so a cent-short balance FAILS the assertion. The tolerance is in fact tighter than every surrounding constraint: CSSRTradingEngine::SaveInto writes balance_check with SetDouble(...,2) and leg realised amounts with DoubleToString(...,6), and CSSRTradingEngine::RestoreFrom raises its own disagreement warning at MathAbs(want_balance - m_balance) > 0.01 - i.e. the test is stricter than production. Impact of the residual gap is a sub-cent discrepancy below the 2-digit display precision of money in this build, and T12.3 independently asserts warn == "" so the engine's own balance_check would also have to agree. Word choice in a comment, not a defect.

The observable wrongness is Count()/the panel's 'checkpoints' figure over-reporting, and the reduced depth.

votes.reason: SpreadFor is unconditional inside Synthesize (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:123) and SynthesizeClose (197), and counts a call, not a bar. EmitWindow re-reads and re-synthesises the clock's own bar on every pump: bar_lo=SSRBarOpenMsc(lo) with lo=emitted+1 (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:380), ReadBars returns that bar (383), the skip loop `< bar_lo` does not exclude it (408), Synthesize/SynthesizeClose runs (440-442), ticks are trimmed to (lo,hi] afterwards (461-470) and the cursor advances to hi (523-531) - so at 1x with InpPumpMs=40 the same minute is synthesised ~1500 times. Nothing resets the counters in the host (ResetSpreadCounters has only a QA-smoke caller), so ReportSpreadOnce trips its `total < 120` gate (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2260) within ~5 s of the first bar and prints 'from the data on N of the first M bars' with N/M counting synthesis calls, and SpreadAverage (sum/recorded) is pump-weighted.
votes.corrected_claim: Correct except that WidestRecordedSpread is a running maximum and so is NOT distorted by the repeated counting; the distortion is in BarsWithRecordedSpread/BarsWithFixedSpread (the 'N of the first M bars' wording) and in AverageRecordedSpread, which becomes a pump-weighted rather than bar-weighted mean.

votes.reason: Confirmed from source. SpreadFor increments m_bars_recorded or m_bars_fixed unconditionally (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:54-67) and is called once per Synthesize (123) / SynthesizeClose (197). In EmitWindow the window is (emitted+1, now], so while the clock stays inside one minute bar_lo == bar_hi == that bar's open, ReadBars returns the same bar, the 'already consumed' skip loop cannot drop it (SSRToMsc(bar.time) == bar_lo, not < bar_lo, SSR_ReplayController.mqh:380-410), and Synthesize is called again on it (441-442) even on pumps whose ticks are all trimmed away by the (lo,hi] filter (461-470). At 40 ms pumps and 1x that is ~1500 counts for one bar. Consequence in the host is exactly as described: ReportSpreadOnce fires at total >= 120 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2260) after a few seconds inside the first bar or two, and then prints 'N of the first M bars' with N/M in the hundreds; the counters are also exposed as SpreadBarsRecorded/Fixed/Average/Widest on the controller. No behavioural impact beyond the diagnostic, but the diagnostic is the one the author instructs users to send.
votes.corrected_claim: Same defect, with a sharper worst case than pump-weighting of the average: because the threshold is reached inside the first one or two bars, the recorded==0 branch can print 'NO bar in the first 1500 carried a recorded spread ... This history has no spread in it' on the strength of a single bar whose spread field happened to be 0 - i.e. the line can state the opposite of the truth, not merely an inflated count. (Within a constant speed the average itself is roughly unbiased, since every bar is re-counted a similar number of times; it skews only across speed changes and stepping.)

votes.reason: The inflation is real. After a pump the cursor sits at hi, the next pump's lo=hi+1 is still inside the same minute, bar_lo=SSRBarOpenMsc(lo) is that bar's open, the skip loop at SSR_ReplayController.mqh:408 cannot drop it (its time == bar_lo), and Synthesize/SynthesizeClose call SpreadFor unconditionally (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:123, 197), so the counters advance once per pump rather than once per bar. Consequently ReportSpreadOnce's 120-sample threshold (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2259) is met inside the FIRST M1 bar and the printed 'N of the first M bars' are pump counts. Impact is a wrong diagnostic number only: the spread actually applied to each tick is still that bar's own, so no money arithmetic changes, and the qualitative verdict the line exists to give (does this history carry a spread at all) survives unless the very first bars differ from the rest - MqlRates.spread is normally populated uniformly or not at all. Downgraded to LOW: a misleading support line, not a defect the trader's account can feel.
votes.corrected_claim: BarsWithRecordedSpread/BarsWithFixedSpread count synthesis calls, so they inflate by roughly pumps-per-bar and the spread report fires inside the first bar while claiming 'the first M bars'; the average/widest become pump-weighted. The spread applied to each emitted tick remains correct, so this is a reporting defect, not an execution one.

votes.reason: The loop is as quoted (SSR_Client.mqh:201-213) and the ack is written only by CSSRPublisher::Poll (SSR_Publisher.mqh:223-247) from the EA's OnTimer, but the load-bearing premise is wrong. MQL5 does not run every program on a chart in one thread: each Expert Advisor (and each script) gets its own execution thread; it is indicators on one symbol that share a thread. A client can never be a second EA on the same chart (one EA per chart), so the co-hosted client is an indicator or script, and neither shares the replay EA's thread. The EA's OnTimer therefore keeps running while the client spins, and with EventSetMillisecondTimer(InpPumpMs) at the default 40 ms (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:78, 1574) the ack lands roughly an order of magnitude inside the 500 ms default, so "cmd.ack is never written" and "every Play/Pause/Step/Buy returns SSR_RC_REFUSED" do not follow. What remains is the documented trade-off the comment at 211-212 already owns: the spin burns a core for up to timeout_ms and, in an indicator, occupies that symbol's indicator thread for the same interval.
votes.corrected_claim: CSSRClient::Send busy-waits without yielding, so a client burns a core for up to timeout_ms and, inside an indicator, blocks that symbol's shared indicator thread for the wait. It does not starve the replay EA: the EA runs in its own thread and Poll() writes the ack from OnTimer every InpPumpMs (40 ms default), well inside the 500 ms timeout.

So the guard at line 176 can never fire across builds, and CanReuse accepts any earlier build's manifest once origin and range agree. SSR_Types.mqh:35 defines SSR_VERSION as "0.1.0" and `git log -S'define SSR_VERSION'` on that file returns only the initial commit dc87fa3, while the stamp that actually moves lives separately (SSR_Build.mqh:22, "v125 2026-09-12") and never enters the manifest - SSRSeedManifest::Init copies only SSR_VERSION (SSR_SeedCache.mqh:43) and Save writes only that (112). So the guard at 176-177 can never fire for any build of this program, and a manifest plus custom symbol written by any earlier build is honoured whenever origin and range agree. votes.reason: The mechanism is real but the stated frequency is wrong. Confirmed from source: CSSRMarketView::OnTicks keeps only ticks[count-1] (SSR_MarketView.mqh:191-198), the OnTick hook takes no parameters (SSR_IStrategy.mqh:266), and CSSRStrategyHost calls OnTick once per OnTicks per strategy while incrementing m_tick_calls once there too — so everything but the last tick of a batch is invisible and TickCalls() counts invocations, not ticks. What is NOT true is "exactly one OnTick per M1 bar at the default". The controller publishes only the ticks that fall inside the pump window (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:459-492: ticks outside lo..hi are dropped before the segment is formed, and a segment is only published when keep > 0), and the synthesizer spreads InpTicksPerBar ticks evenly across the minute (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147). At 40 ms pumps (InpPumpMs=40) the window is 40 ms x speed, so below roughly 200x it is shorter than the ~8.5 s tick spacing and each batch carries a single tick — the strategy does see each synthetic price, including the bar's high and low. The collapse to one price per bar happens only where a batch spans a whole minute: MAX speed / catch-up, or a step-a-candle command.
votes.corrected_claim: Whenever a published batch carries more than one tick — MAX/very high speed, catch-up, or a candle step — CSSRMarketView retains only the last tick's bid/ask, so the strategy's parameterless OnTick cannot see the intrabar excursion in that batch, and TickCalls() counts batches rather than ticks. At ordinary speeds each batch holds one tick, so the per-tick hook does fire per synthetic tick and the intrabar prices are visible.

votes.reason: The delivery granularity is provable. SSR_ReplayController.mqh:502-511 publishes one bar context then one tick SEGMENT per M1 bar, each segment being that bar's synthesised ticks; CSSRStrategyHost::OnTicks calls m_strat[i].OnTick() exactly once per OnTicks invocation (SSR_StrategyHost.mqh:209-210). So with InpTicksPerBar=8 a strategy gets one OnTick per M1 bar, not per tick, and CSSRMarketView::OnTicks (SSR_MarketView.mqh:190-197) keeps only ticks[count-1], so the intrabar SEQUENCE is unrecoverable. Two parts of the evidence are wrong, hence the correction: the bar's high and low are NOT lost - PublishBar runs before PublishSegment and CSSRMarketView::OnBarContext (172-188) stores the full MqlRates, so ctx.market.High/Low(PERIOD_M1, 0) reaches them; and m_tick_calls is incremented inside the per-strategy loop, so it counts batches x enabled strategies, not batches.
votes.corrected_claim: OnTick is delivered once per published per-bar segment (one per M1 bar at SYNTHETIC_TICK), not once per synthesised tick, so a strategy cannot manage tick-by-tick inside a bar and cannot know the order in which the bar's prices occurred - although the bar's OHLC itself is reachable via ctx.market.Bar/High/Low(PERIOD_M1, 0), published immediately before the segment. TickCalls() counts OnTick invocations (batches x enabled strategies) while ToString() labels them "ticks".

reasons: The mechanism is real but the stated frequency is wrong. What is NOT true is "exactly one OnTick per M1 bar at the default". The controller publishes only the ticks that fall inside the pump window (SSR_ReplayController.mqh:459-492: ticks outside lo..hi are dropped before the segment is formed, and a segment is only published when keep > 0), and the synthesizer spreads InpTicksPerBar ticks evenly across the minute (SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:147). At 40 ms pumps (InpPumpMs=40) the window is 40 ms x speed, so below roughly 200x it is shorter than the ~8.5 s tick spacing and each batch carries a single tick — the strategy does see each synthetic price, including the bar's high and low. The collapse to one price per bar happens only where a batch spans a whole minute: MAX speed / catch-up, or a step-a-candle command.

votes.reason: Traced end to end. SSRPendingFor's on-the-price refusal and the limit/stop split both measure against bid (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:113, 120-124), while the long pending's trigger in CheckPendings is the ask (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:337: BUY_STOP hit when m_ask >= request_price). The only caller passes min_dist = pt * 2.0 (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:1010), and neither OpenPendingWithRisk (:783-801) nor Open (:705-739) imposes any minimum distance from the market on a pending — Open just stores request_price and returns. So any long entry in (bid + 2 points, ask) is classified BUY_STOP and is already triggered when placed; with the default InpSpreadPoints = 20 (SSReplayStandalone.mq5:76) that is an 18-point window, and the fill takes FillPrice(long, true) = ask + slippage, worse than the drawn line — exactly what the refusal text claims to prevent. The short side is not symmetric: entry above bid becomes SELL_LIMIT (triggers on bid >= entry), which does not fire immediately. LOW is right: the position is virtual and bounded by the spread.

Both halves check out in source. SSRPendingFor uses bid for the on-the-price refusal (SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:113) and for the limit-vs-stop decision (120-124), while CSSRTradingEngine::CheckPendings triggers BUY_STOP on ask >= request_price (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:337) and fills at FillPrice(long,true) (345). Both call sites pass min_dist = pt*2.0 (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:296 and 1010), so any long entry in (bid + 2 points, ask) passes the guard, is classified BUY_STOP, and is triggered by the very next tick - and the engine's ask is bid + spread whenever the bar has none (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:604-607, InpSpreadPoints default 20). The window is 18 points wide at that default, and the asymmetry is right: BUY_LIMIT (ask <= price), SELL_LIMIT (bid >= price) and SELL_STOP (bid <= price) cannot trigger immediately from inside the spread. LOW because the fill is at the correct ask and only mislabels a market order as pending; it closes if the guard is widened to cover the ask side.

The asymmetry is provable and I verified both halves. SSRPendingFor compares the entry against bid for the on-the-price refusal (113) and for the limit/stop split (120-124), while CheckPendings triggers a BUY_STOP on ask >= request_price (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:337). Callers pass min_dist = pt*2.0 (SSR_GroupPort.mqh:295, 1010), and the default synthetic spread is 20 points (host:76), so any long entry in (bid + 2pt, ask] is classified BUY_STOP and satisfies its own trigger on the very next tick - exactly what the refusal text at 113-118 claims to prevent. Money angle, which the finding does not spell out: the lot was sized from the entry LINE to the stop (OpenPendingWithRisk with en), yet the fill is FillPrice(is_long,true) at ask plus adverse slippage, so the realised stop distance - and therefore the money at risk - exceeds the requested risk percent by up to the spread; risk_at_entry is recomputed from the actual fill (SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:351-354), so the statement's R stays honest. The short side is sound (SELL_STOP triggers on bid <= price and is classified off bid, so it cannot self-trigger). Kept at LOW: the band is only spread-wide, it needs the entry line dragged into the spread, and the trade is still executed and accounted correctly.

Because the size came from the entry line but the fill is at ask, the position also carries slightly more money at risk than the requested percent (risk_at_entry is recomputed from the fill, so reporting stays honest). votes.reason: Traced the whole path and found no clamp. OnInit does ArrayResize(g_samp, InpWindow) then ArrayInitialize with no validation (lines 34-35) and starts the timer (line 42); OnTimer's first buffer statement is the indexed write g_samp[g_head] (line 65) followed immediately by % InpWindow (line 66). LOW is right: it needs a deliberate misconfiguration of a dev-only probe whose default is 2000.

With InpWindow=0 the indexed write into a zero-length dynamic array is an out-of-range critical error, which is established MQL5 semantics, and it stops the program before the modulus is ever evaluated - so the 'divides by zero' ordering is wrong. The negative case is also mis-described: ArrayResize with a negative size fails and leaves size 0, so the same out-of-range write occurs, but % with a negative modulus is well defined and is not a fault. Reaching any of this requires a deliberately invalid input to a spike probe, and whether the terminal reports or silently removes the indicator is runtime behaviour - hence at most POTENTIAL_RISK, LOW.
